title: Set up the shared workspace and the approved libraries
what: One workspace in which every part of Policy Plus is built, with only the approved libraries for reading policy template text, unpacking the Microsoft package and wiring services.
why: Without one agreed set of tools and libraries each part drifts and the program cannot be built and checked the same way everywhere.

criteria.says: Given a fresh checkout, when a developer runs the install and the verify command for any layer, then the same task names (lint, typecheck, test, build) exist and succeed for every layer.
Given the workspace is checked on a machine that is not Windows, when the build and tests run, then they succeed using the stand-in versions of the Windows-only carriers.
Given a required setting is missing, when the service or the web app starts, then it stops at start with a message naming the missing setting.
Given the dependency list, when it is checked, then it holds only the stack's libraries plus the approved XML reader and zip reader, and no second state or validation library.
Given a policy template file with well-formed text, when it is read with the approved XML reader, then its values come back and are checked against a schema afterwards.
Given the Microsoft template package as a standard zip, when it is unpacked with the approved zip reader, then its files are listed and readable without any native build step.

open: Should existing registry settings of the old program be imported once into the new preference store?

title: Set up the test approach with fixtures and a real database
what: The way every part is tested: fixture text for template, policy and registry files, a real PostgreSQL for data tests, stand-ins for Windows carriers and tests named after the legacy rule.
why: Rules and stories are only trusted if they can be proven the same way on any machine.

criteria.says: Given the test command for domain, contracts, database or service, when it runs, then it uses fixture text for ADMX, ADML, POL and REG files.
Given a database test, when it runs, then a real PostgreSQL is started by the test task and no mocked client is used.

Given a test of a Windows-only carrier, when it runs on a machine that is not Windows, then it runs against the stand-in behind its port and the few Windows-gated tests are skipped with a stated reason.
Given a rule or story that is built, when its test is listed, then the title names the legacy rule it proves.
Given an end-to-end test, when it is written for a story, then it exists and fails before the code it tests is added.

title: Keep behaviour in code, tests and short agent notes
what: A place for each kind of knowledge: behaviour in typed code and tests, rationale in the plan, and only what tools do not show in the agent notes of each layer.
why: Knowledge kept in checked code cannot silently drift from the product.

criteria.says: Given a contract schema, when the OpenAPI document is generated, then the documentation text on the schema appears in it.
Given a domain folder, when it is opened, then it offers a typed index of what it exports and no prose readme.
Given a test title, when it is read, then it cites the legacy rule it proves.
Given the agent notes of a layer, when they are checked, then they hold only what code and tools do not show and copy no decision rationale from the plan.

title: Define the contract schemas and generate the interface document
what: Every request, answer and failure between the screens and the service is described once as a schema, and the interface document is generated from it.
why: Screens and service cannot disagree about what is exchanged when there is one source.

criteria.says: Given any request, response or error, when the contracts are inspected, then it is defined once as a schema and not written by hand elsewhere.
Given the service contract, when the build runs, then the OpenAPI document is generated from it and no hand-written copy exists.
Given a missing domain, no network or no administrator rights, when the service answers, then the answer is a named outcome in the schema and not an error response.
Given the contracts package, when its dependencies are checked, then it depends only on the effect library and imports no other workspace package.

title: Build the policy rules as a pure layer with named ports
what: The policy rules live in one folder per capability, take data in and return data, and meet the outside world only through named ports.
why: Rules that touch no disk, clock or registry can be tested with fixture text anywhere.

criteria.says: Given any function in the domain layer, when it runs in a test, then it reads no file, clock, random value or environment and returns data or an Effect of data.
Given an outside system the rules need, when the domain is inspected, then it is declared as a port there and implemented only in the service.
Given the domain layer, when its folders are listed, then there is one folder per capability named as in the plan, and shared helpers sit in folders named for what they do, never utils or common.
Given ADMX, ADML, CMTX, POL or REG text, when it enters the domain, then it is parsed at the edge into schema-checked values and later rules never see raw text or bytes.
Given malformed input, when it is parsed, then it is refused at the edge with a named failure and nothing downstream runs.

title: Set up the preference store with committed migrations
what: A PostgreSQL store for remembered choices (language, definitions folder, offers considered), changed only through committed migrations and reached through query functions.
why: The old program remembered choices in a Windows registry key; the new one needs a store that fits the confirmed architecture and keeps history of every change.

terms.name: Preference store
terms.means: The place where Policy Plus remembers a person's own choices, such as language and definitions folder; it is not where policy settings themselves are kept.

criteria.says: Given a remembered choice such as the language or the definitions folder, when it is saved and the program restarts, then the same choice is read back from the preference store.
Given the program runs, when it starts, then it neither reads nor writes the old registry settings key.
Given a change to the data layout, when it is made, then it exists as a committed migration and no merged migration is edited afterwards.
Given a query function, when it returns, then it gives plain data in the contract's shape and never a table object.
Given an empty database, when the migrations are applied and the database tests run, then they pass against a real PostgreSQL.

title: Serve the HTTP interface with thin handlers
what: A local service on the person's machine that answers the screens through the contract, deciding nothing itself.
why: Keeping rules out of handlers keeps them in the tested pure layer.

criteria.says: Given a request, when a handler runs, then it only decodes with the contract, calls domain functions and carriers, and encodes the answer.
Given a request that breaks a rule, when it is answered, then the decision comes from the domain layer and no rule is found in the handler.
Given each outside system (file system, registry, directory, download), when the service is assembled, then each is one layer implementing a domain port.
Given a test run or a machine that is not Windows, when the service starts, then the stand-in for each Windows carrier is used.

title: Read and write folders and policy files on the person's machine
what: The service reads, lists and writes folders and files (policy files, template folders, export targets) directly so the browser never touches the disk.
why: The program must edit real policy files at fixed Windows paths, which a browser cannot do.

criteria.says: Given a chosen folder, when the screen asks for its contents, then the service lists and reads them and the web app never reads the disk itself.
Given a save of a policy file, when it runs, then the content goes to a temporary file that is renamed over the target.
Given a save that fails part way, when the person looks at the target, then the earlier file is unchanged and the failure is reported.
Given ADMX and ADML files in the chosen folders, when the definitions are loaded, then the service reads their text and passes it to the domain parsers, which return schema-checked values.
Given a policy source with a comment file beside it, when comments are read or saved, then the service reads and writes the CMTX file in place and the domain encodes and decodes it.

title: Read and write registry policies and user hives safely
what: The service reads and writes policy keys, and loads and unloads user hives, through one registry port that the rules see only as plain data.
why: Registry editing must work on Home editions without a compiled add-on and must not allow typed keys to run commands.

criteria.says: Given a policy key, when it is read or written, then the service uses the built-in Windows tools behind one registry port and the domain sees only data.
Given a user hive that is not loaded, when the person chooses it, then it is loaded and later unloaded through the same port.
Given a typed key path or account name, when it is used, then it is checked against the contract schema first and passed to the tool as separate arguments, never as a built command string.
Given machine policy is written without administrator rights, when the write is refused, then the answer is a named no-rights outcome.

title: Look up accounts and policy locations in the Active Directory domain
what: The service resolves user and group accounts and their profile and policy-object locations from the machine's own directory tools, or says the domain is unavailable.
why: Only the person's machine is joined to the domain with their credentials, and a missing domain is a normal outcome.

criteria.says: Given a reachable domain, when an account is looked up, then its profile and policy-object locations are returned as plain data.
Given no reachable domain, when an account is looked up, then the answer is a named unavailable outcome and not an error.
Given a typed account name, when the lookup runs, then the name is validated first and passed as separate arguments.

title: Download and unpack the Microsoft policy template package
what: The service downloads the package from the Microsoft download site, unpacks it into the chosen folder and reports progress and failure.
why: The package must be unpacked into a Windows folder, which a browser cannot do, and having no internet is a normal outcome.

criteria.says: Given internet access, when a download starts, then the service fetches the package, unpacks it into the chosen folder and reports progress to the screen.
Given no internet access or a refused download, when it is attempted, then the answer is a named failure outcome and the folder is left as it was.
Given the web app, when a download is wanted, then it asks the service and never calls the Microsoft site itself.

title: Build the shared interface components with Storybook
what: A library of shared screen components that take data and callbacks only, shown in Storybook, using the approved design tokens.
why: One visual language and proven accessibility across all screens.

criteria.says: Given a component, when it is used, then it takes data and callbacks only and never calls the service or the router.
Given a component, when Storybook is opened, then a story covers each of its states and an accessibility scan of it passes.
Given a style, when it is added, then it uses the Tailwind 4 tokens and shadcn on Base UI primitives and adds no new colour, spacing or icon set.

title: Build the web app shell, data access, messages and forms
what: The screens' frame: server-rendered routes that fetch through the generated client, show every visible text as a translatable message, and validate forms with the contract.
why: Screens must stay unprivileged, speak the person's chosen language and reject the same input as the service.

criteria.says: Given a screen, when it fetches data, then it uses a client generated from the contract through TanStack Query with no hand-written calls or copied response types.
Given the product language is switched, when a screen is shown, then every visible text changes and policy text from definitions stays as data, untranslated.
Given a form with invalid input, when it is submitted, then the client rejects it with the same rules the service would apply.
Given a page is rendered on the server, when it loads data, then it asks the service over HTTP and itself reads no disk or registry.

title: Set up end-to-end tests with accessibility scans
what: A Playwright suite that drives the running product with stand-in Windows carriers, scans every page and finds elements the way a person does.
why: Stories are proven by behaviour, accessibility is a gate and tests stay deterministic without Windows.

criteria.says: Given a story's acceptance criteria, when its test is committed, then it is committed before the code and fails first.
Given the suite runs, when it starts, then it uses the real service with the stand-in Windows carriers.
Given any page visited in a test, when it is scanned for accessibility, then any violation fails the test.
Given an element a test uses, when it is found, then it is selected by role and accessible name and not by style class or test id unless it has no role.

title: Stamp the program with its Git version at build time
what: The build records the current Git version in a value the service reports, in place of generating a version source file.
why: The new build has no compile step needing a generated file, and a committed generated file goes stale.

criteria.says: Given a build from a Git commit, when the service is asked for its version, then it reports that commit's version.
Given the repository, when it is checked, then no generated version source file is committed.

title: Share one set of code checks and commit rules across layers
what: One shared setup for linting, formatting, unused-code checks, markdown checks and commit messages, run before every commit.
why: One policy for every layer, and early failure beats failing in CI.

criteria.says: Given a layer, when its checks are configured, then it extends the shared setup and adds no local lint or format rule.
Given a commit message that is not a conventional commit, when the commit is made, then it is refused.
Given a commit, when it is made, then the hooks run lint, format and the checks of the affected layers, and skipping hooks is not allowed.
Given any layer, when the unused-code check runs, then it reports no unused files, exports or dependencies.

title: Load policy definitions from a folder or single files
what: Read the administrative template and language files from a chosen folder, or add a single template file, and build the policies and categories people browse.
why: People can only browse and edit policies once their definitions are loaded, and they need to know when something in them could not be used.

terms.name: Definitions
terms.means: The administrative template and language files that describe the policies; not the settings people choose.

criteria.says: Given a folder of template and language files, when the person loads it, then the files are read from that folder and handed on as parsed documents, and the person's own machine is the only place read.

Given a load that finds no problems, when it finishes, then nothing is shown; given problems, then the person sees "Errors were encountered while adding administrative templates to the workspace." with each problem and is asked "Continue trying to use this workspace?" only where a choice is wanted.
Given policies already loaded, when the person adds one template file, then that file alone is added to them, the structures are rebuilt, and a refused file is reported as one failure.

title: Show the category tree and the policies of the chosen area
what: Present the categories of the loaded definitions as a tree with icons, visibility, selection, and a choice of user or computer area.
why: People find a policy by walking the categories, so the tree must show the right ones and keep their place as it changes.

terms.name: Empty category
terms.means: A category with no visible policy and no visible subcategory; not a category that is missing.

criteria.says: Given a category, when its icon is chosen, then it is orphaned first, empty next, and normal otherwise.
Given empty categories are switched off, when a category has no visible policy and no visible subcategory, then it is not visible; when they are switched on, every category is visible.
Given the loaded definitions, when the tree is shown, then only visible categories appear, each with its icon and its visible subcategories below it, sorted.
Given the category shown in the right pane changes, when the tree updates, then its selection follows that category.
Given the tree is rebuilt from newly loaded definitions, when it finishes, then nothing is selected and the information pane shows the empty state.
Given a category is selected in the tree, when the person selects it, then it becomes the current category and any selected policy is cleared.
Given the "Empty Categories" menu, when the person switches empty categories on or off, then the view moves to the nearest visible category.
Given the area choice, when it is "User", then user policies show; "Computer", computer policies; any other choice, both.

Given the list is rebuilt, when the earlier policy is still in the category shown and visible, then it is selected and revealed and the earlier top row is put back if the list still has that many rows; otherwise nothing is selected.

title: Read and write policy files byte for byte
what: Turn the bytes of a policy file into entries and entries back into bytes, with its signature, version, text and number encodings, ordering and duplicate handling.
why: Policy files are what Windows reads, so a file saved here must be read back exactly and a bad file must be refused with a clear message.

terms.name: Policy file
terms.means: A saved file of policy settings for one machine or user; not the definitions that describe the policies.

criteria.says: Given text in a policy file, when it is read, then it stops at its first empty character, and a multiple-string value ends at its first empty string.

Given a stored value, when it is read back, then it is text for text and expandable text, a 32-bit or 64-bit number for numbers, a list of strings for multiple strings, and raw bytes for every other type.
Given a file whose format version is not 1, when it is read, then it is refused with 'Unknown (newer) version of POL format'.
Given a file that does not start with the 'PReg' signature, when it is read, then it is refused with 'Missing PReg signature'.
Given an extra empty character after a value name, when the file is read, then it is skipped, as Microsoft's documentation allows.
Given entries, when the file is saved, then they are written in alphabetical order so a key-clearing marker comes before the values it clears.
Given a multiple-string value, when it is saved, then each string is followed by an empty character and one more empty character closes the list.
Given a 64-bit number, when it is saved, then it is 8 bytes, lowest byte first.
Given a 32-bit number, when it is saved, then it is 4 bytes, lowest byte first.
Given text, when it is saved, then it is written in two-byte characters followed by a closing empty character.
Given a value, when it is saved, then text, expandable text, 32-bit and 64-bit numbers and multiple strings are stored by their stated type and every other type as raw bytes with that type.
Given the same key and value name twice in a file, when it is read, then the later entry wins, names match without regard to letter case, and the first spelling seen is kept for saving.

title: Hold a policy file's settings in memory and answer questions about them
what: Keep the entries of one policy file and answer whether a value is present, read it, set it, forget it, mark it for deletion or clear a key.
why: Applying policies and checking what a file says depend on these answers being exact, including what is marked for deletion.

terms.name: Marked for deletion
terms.means: A value the file says should be removed on the machine; not a value that is merely absent.

criteria.says: Given a policy file, when a value is checked, then it counts as marked for deletion when a deletion marker, a clear-all marker or a delete-values list names it, regardless of case, and a later-sorting value of that name cancels the deletion.
Given a key, when its values are listed, then marker entries are left out unless the caller asks for them.
Given a value that is absent or marked for deletion, when it is read, then nothing is given.
Given a value, when its presence is asked, then it counts as present only if it is stored and not marked for deletion.
Given an expected deletion marker, number or text, when presence is tested, then it is present if marked, an equal whole number, or equal text; a value of the wrong kind is not present.
Given a value, when it is marked for deletion, then anything held under that name is dropped and a marker holding 32 is added unless already marked or its key is cleared.
Given a value, when it is set, then it replaces any value under that name and a deletion marker for the name is kept.
Given a value, when it is forgotten, then both the value and its marker are removed so the policy says nothing about it.
Given a key, when it is cleared, then all values and markers under it are dropped and a single clear-all marker is stored.

title: Read and write the machine's live policy settings
what: Read, write, delete and clear the live policy settings of the machine, check the root names and test whether they can be written.
why: People apply policies straight to the machine, so this source must behave as the machine's own settings do.

terms.name: Live settings
terms.means: The policy settings currently in force on the machine; not a saved policy file.

criteria.says: Given the machine's settings are reached from the person's own machine, when they are read or changed, then the service does so on that machine only and the web app never does.
Given the live settings, when a value is checked for deletion, then it is never reported as marked for deletion.

Given a key and a value name, when presence is asked, then it is present when the key exists and, unless the name is empty, the key lists that name regardless of case; an empty name means the key itself.
Given a missing key, when a value is read, then nothing is given; signed numbers come back as the unsigned numbers policies use and environment variables in text are not expanded.
Given an unsigned 32-bit or 64-bit number, when it is saved, then it is stored as the signed number with the same bits and the key is created if missing.
Given a key that does not exist, when a value is deleted, then nothing happens and no error is shown.
Given a value, when it is forgotten, then it is deleted, since a pending deletion cannot be remembered.
Given a key, when it is cleared, then every value in it is deleted but the key and its subkeys stay; forgetting a key's clearance does nothing.
Given a settings source, when a test value cannot be written under Software\Policies and removed again, then the source is read-only.

Given a source path, when it does not start with HKCU, HKEY_CURRENT_USER, HKU, HKEY_USERS, HKLM or HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE in any case, then it is refused with "The root key is not valid."; otherwise the path is opened and created if missing.

title: Open another user's stored settings file as a source
what: Load a user's stored settings file into the machine under a temporary name and unload it when the source is released.
why: People can edit the policies of a user who is not signed in, and the machine must be left as it was.

terms.name: User hive
terms.means: A user's stored settings file; not the live settings of the signed-in user.

criteria.says: Given a user's stored settings file, when it is used as a source, then it is loaded under a fresh temporary name after the backup and restore rights are switched on, by the service on the person's machine.
Given the file cannot be opened after loading, when the source is used, then it silently becomes an empty read-only scratch source.
Given a source is closed, when it is a mounted user hive, then it is unloaded and the result tells whether that succeeded; every other kind of source closes successfully.

title: Export settings to a registry text file
what: Collect the settings destined for an exported registry text file, limited to a branch, and refuse every read or check.
why: People can save policies as a registry text file to share or import, and must be told plainly when a file cannot be read back.

terms.name: Registry export file
terms.means: A registry text file made to import settings elsewhere; not a policy file.

criteria.says: Given a registry export file, when a value is checked for deletion, then the request fails with 'not implemented'.
Given a registry export file, when a value is read, then the request fails with 'not implemented'.
Given a registry export file, when a key's values are listed, then the request fails with 'not implemented'.
Given a registry export file, when presence is asked, then the request fails with 'not implemented'.
Given a registry export file, when a value is forgotten, then the request fails with 'not implemented'.
Given a value is saved, when a branch is set and its key lies outside it, then it is ignored; with no branch every key is accepted, and any value under that name is replaced.
Given a value is deleted, when a branch is set and the key lies outside it or the key is already marked for removal, then it is ignored; otherwise the value is recorded as deleted.
Given a key is cleared, when a branch is set and it lies outside, then it is ignored; otherwise its earlier entries are replaced by a key-removal entry.

open: Applying a newer policy file over an older one to a registry export file fails for any dropped value under a policy branch; should the target keep this failure or support it?

title: Apply one policy file's changes onto another source
what: When a policy file's changes are applied to another source, each entry is saved, deleted or cleared as the file says, and values a newer file dropped are forgotten.
why: Administrators can bring one policy file's settings into another source and trust that deletions and removals carry over exactly.

terms.name: Marker-style entry
terms.means: A policy file entry whose name starts with '**' and tells the program to delete or clear something instead of storing a value; it is not a stored setting.

criteria.says: Given a policy file with entries, when its changes are applied to another source, then an entry is saved only if it has a value name that is not empty and does not start with '**', and the saved value keeps its letter case and type; other marker-style entries and entries with an empty value name are skipped without a message.

Given an entry starting '**deletekeys', when the changes are applied, then each key in its semicolon-separated list under the entry's key is cleared, using lower-case names, and only that key's own values go, not its subkeys.
Given an entry named '**deletevalues', when the changes are applied, then each value in its semicolon-separated list is deleted, using lower-case names.
Given an entry named '**del.' followed by a value name, when the changes are applied, then that value is deleted, using the lower-case key and value names.

Given an entry starting '**delvals', when the changes are applied, then the whole key is cleared, using the lower-case key name; entries are applied in sorted order so clear-all entries come before values, and clearing a live registry key removes only that key's own values.

Given a newer policy file applied over an older one, when the older file held values the newer one dropped, then those values are forgotten in the target, but only when they sit under the three policy branches of the registry.

title: Provide an empty scratch source and policy files on the machine
what: A Scratch space source starts empty and is never saved, and policy files and their folders on the computer are read, created empty when missing, and opened for reading and writing.
why: People can practise or prepare changes without touching anything, and can point the program at real policy files without them having to exist first.

terms.name: Scratch space
terms.means: A source that starts empty, can be changed and is never saved; it is not a file or the registry.

criteria.says: Given a Scratch space source is chosen, when the person works with it, then it starts empty, can be changed, and is never saved anywhere.

Given the policy file of a POL file source, the local Group Policy or a per-user Group Policy does not exist, when the source is opened, then it is created empty with its folder and treated as writable, so a mistyped SID creates a new folder and empty file under the per-user policy folder; if creation fails, an empty read-only source is used and no error is shown.

Given a POL file, the local Group Policy or a per-user Group Policy that already has a file, when the source is opened, then the file is loaded and is writable only when it can be opened for reading and writing; otherwise it can be viewed but its changes cannot be committed.

title: Work out where each source's policy and comment files live
what: From a source's kind and the detail given, the program decides the location of its policy file and of its comment file.
why: Every source reads and saves its settings and comments in the right place without the person having to type paths.

criteria.says: Given a source of a certain kind, when its policy file location is needed, then Local GPO uses the Registry.pol of the system's local Group Policy (user or machine folder) and its gpt.ini, a per-user GPO uses the folder named by the person's SID under GroupPolicyUsers, a POL file and a user hive use the path given, and Scratch space has none.

Given a source, when its comment file location is needed, then it sits beside the source's file: the POL file or hive path with the extension changed to .cmtx; for Local GPO or a per-user GPO a file named comment.cmtx in the same folder; for the registry a file under the person's local application data folder (one for user, one for machine); and Scratch space has none, so comments are unavailable.

title: Open the user and computer sources and remember them
what: The program closes open sources, opens the user and computer sources from the person's choice or the defaults, remembers the last choice, and falls back to the defaults when the saved sources cannot be reached.
why: People always return to the sources they were working with, and never end up stuck when those sources have gone.

criteria.says: Given sources are already open, when new sources are opened, then the open ones are closed first; unsaved changes are discarded for sources backed by a POL file (local Group Policy files, a chosen POL file, a per-user Group Policy object) and for the empty source, while a registry source applies changes at once and a user hive file is applied when closed, so those lose nothing.
Given first start with no saved policy sources, when the program opens, then both the user source and the computer source open as the local Group Policy files (Local GPO) with no extra location.

Given the policy sources dialog opens with the last-used sources, when it shows, then each side is set to the remembered kind (Local GPO, Registry, POL file, Scratch space, and for users also per-user GPO or user hive), and the registry path, file name, SID or hive path is filled in only for kinds that carry one.

Given the previously saved sources cannot be opened, when the program starts them, then the person is told "The previous policy sources are not accessible. The defaults will be loaded.", both sources are saved as Local GPO and opened quietly, and only the source type is reset while any saved location text stays.

title: Keep and save policy comments for each source
what: Comments are kept per policy and area, found when wanted, and saved to the comment file beside the source, which is read and written with a text id and prefix for every comment.
why: Administrators can leave notes on policies and trust them to be saved with the source and read back intact.

criteria.says: Given a policy and an area, when its comment is wanted, then it is empty when the source has no comment file or no comment for the policy, and otherwise the saved text.

Given a source, when its comments are loaded, then they are used only if it has a comment file location; the folder is created if missing, an existing file is loaded, a missing file gives no comments yet, and any failure leaves that source without comments.
Given a source's comment list exists, when comments are saved, then the list is written to its comment file location even when empty, and a source without comment support has no list and is skipped.

Given a comment file, when it is read, then it is refused as unreadable and the source's comments become unavailable if it has no comment-definitions section, a namespace entry without a prefix, a comment without a policy reference, a text without an id, or a repeated prefix, policy reference or text id.

Given a comment file, when the comments are read, then none can be read if any comment's policy reference has no colon or a prefix that is not declared, its text is not written as "$(resource.<id>)", its text id is missing, or two comments resolve to the same policy.
Given comments held in memory, when they are saved, then every comment and text is written into the target file in schema version 1.0, replacing what the file held before.

Given comments being saved, when the file is written, then each comment gets its own text id built from the policy's namespace, policy name and a running number, and each distinct namespace gets a prefix made from its name (dots turned into underscores) and the running number.

title: Turn a typed user name into a valid account identifier
what: A user name typed in the user dialog is looked up in the directory to give the account's security identifier (SID), and a typed SID is checked before the dialog closes.
why: People can pick another user's policies by name instead of needing to know a SID, and cannot proceed with an invalid one.

terms.name: SID
terms.means: The security identifier that names one account for Windows; it is not the account's typed user name.

criteria.says: Given a name typed in the user dialog, when the person presses Search, then it is turned into the account's SID; if it cannot be translated, they are told "The name could not be translated to a SID."
Given a name typed but no SID, when the person presses OK, then the name is looked up first and the dialog stays open if no SID results.

Given a SID text, when the person presses OK, then it must be a valid SID or they are told "The SID is not valid. Enter a SID in the lower box, or enter a username in the top box and press Search to translate."; a valid SID is returned and the dialog closes.

title: Settle each policy's state from the evidence in its source
what: Enabled and disabled evidence is counted from the values and lists a source holds for a policy and its options, and each policy's state in an area is settled and given to the screens as plain facts.
why: People see whether each policy is Enabled, Disabled or Not configured in the way Windows would read it.

terms.name: Evidence
terms.means: The settings found in a source that point to a policy being on or off; it is not the policy's final state, which is settled from all of it.

criteria.says: Given a policy with a registry value of its own, when it is read, then it counts as enabled evidence when the value holds its 'on' value (the number 1 when the template gives none) and as disabled evidence when it holds its 'off' value or is marked for deletion when the template gives none.

Given a policy's switched-on and switched-off effects, when they are read, then they come from its enabled and disabled values and lists, where a list entry names a value and optionally its own key, falling back to the list's default key.
Given a policy's lists of on-values and off-values, when they are read, then each value present counts as enabled or disabled evidence, using the list's own key when it names one.
Given a policy's list elements, when they are read, then a list marked for deletion counts as one deleted element, and a list holding any values counts as a present element and cancels that deletion.
Given a number, text, choice or multi-line text element, when it is read, then a value marked for deletion counts as a deleted element and a value that is present counts as a present element.

Given a checkbox element, when it is read, then a value marked for deletion counts as one deleted element; otherwise each present off value (or off-list value) counts a tenth of a deleted element and each present on value (or on-list value) counts one present element, and a checkbox whose template declares no on value or on list adds no present evidence even if it holds 1.

Given the elements of a policy, when evidence is added, then if any element is present the elements add their count to the enabled evidence, and only when none is present do deleted elements add to the disabled evidence.

Given the enabled and disabled evidence, when the state is settled, then the policy is Enabled when enabled exceeds disabled, Disabled when disabled exceeds enabled, Not configured when there is no evidence either way, and Unclear when both are equal and above zero.

Given a policy and an area, when its state is shown, then it reads "Enabled", "Disabled", "Not Configured" or "Unknown", reading the computer source for the computer area and the user source for any other, and the screens receive the state of each policy in the area as plain facts.

open: The rules give the states Not Configured, Not configured, Unclear and Unknown in different places; which exact wording and when 'Unclear' is shown on screen is not settled.

title: Show policy settings as semantic policy text with or without a heading
what: A policy's settings are written as semantic policy text, with the heading 'Policy Plus Semantic Policy' only when the person ticks the option.
why: People can copy just the fragment they need or a complete, labelled text to share.

criteria.says: Given a policy's settings shown as text, when "Include SPOL header" is ticked, then the text starts with the heading "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and a blank line; when it is not ticked, only the fragment is shown.

title: Offer the area choice and reopen the last search results
what: The area list offers exactly three choices and starts on both areas, and the last search results and chosen position can be reopened without a new search until the search is cleared.
why: People start with every policy in view and can return to their results without searching again.

criteria.says: Given the program starts, when the area list shows, then it starts on "User or Computer", the first choice, so both user and computer policies are shown.
Given the area list, when the person opens it, then it offers only "User or Computer", "User" and "Computer", with no free text.

Given no search has been run or it was cleared, when the person opens the results from the main window, then they are told "No search has been run yet, so there are no results to display." and nothing opens.
Given search results exist, when the person chooses "Search Results", then the last results are reopened and no new search starts.
Given the results window is reopened, when the previously selected result is still in the list, then it is selected again.
Given results are held, when the search is cleared, then the results are forgotten and reopening them reports that no search has been run.

title: Read typed numbers within the 32-bit and 64-bit limits
what: Numbers typed for a registry value are read as decimal or marked hexadecimal and held to the range of a 32-bit or 64-bit value.
why: People cannot store a number a registry value cannot hold, and typing mistakes never silently change a value.

criteria.says: Given a number entered for a registry value, when it is read, then it is limited to 0 to 4,294,967,295 for a 32-bit value and to 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 for a 64-bit value.
Given a typed hexadecimal number, when it is too large to fit then the value is set to the largest allowed value, and when the text is not a hexadecimal number the value is left unchanged.

title: Edit the data of a policy value by its kind
what: Let a person change the data of a value in a policy file with the entry that fits its kind: a text box for text, a number box for numbers, a multi-line box for lists of text.
why: Raw editing of a policy file is only safe when each value is edited in a form that matches what it holds, and when kinds the editor cannot handle are refused instead of damaged.

criteria.says: Given a value of a plain or expandable text kind, when the person edits it, then a text box showing its current data is offered.
Given a value of a 32-bit or 64-bit number kind, when the person edits it, then a number box showing its current data is offered.
Given a value that is a list of text, when the person edits it, then a multi-line box showing its current data is offered.
Given a value of any other kind, such as binary, when the person tries to edit it, then they see "This value kind is not supported." and nothing changes.
Given an edit dialog is open, when the person cancels it, then the value keeps its data exactly as it was.
Given the person confirms new data, when the edit is applied, then the value holds the new data, keeps its name and kind, and stays selected.

title: Download the fixed Microsoft policy template package
what: Fetch the one Microsoft package of administrative templates, the Windows 11 September 2026 Update (26H2), into a scratch folder on the person's computer, through the service rather than the browser.
why: People who lack current policy definitions need them from Microsoft without hunting for the right download; a fixed package and secure connections keep the result predictable and safe.

criteria.says: Given the person starts the download, when it runs, then the Windows 11 September 2026 Update (26H2) administrative templates are saved as "W11Admx.msi" in a scratch folder under their local application data.
Given the person wants another version, when they start the download, then no choice of version is offered and the same package is fetched.
Given a download is made, when the connection is opened, then only TLS 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 are accepted and no other protocol is used.
Given the Microsoft site cannot be reached, when the download is started, then the failure is reported as a normal outcome and the screens never contact the site themselves.

open: Should the download still allow TLS 1.0 and 1.1, which are long retired, or only TLS 1.2 and later?

title: Stamp the program with its Git version at build time
what: When the program is built, work out its version from the source history and make it available to the running program, leaving the committed source with an empty version.
why: Support and people reporting problems need to know exactly which build they run, without anyone typing a version by hand.

criteria.says: Given the source history has tags, when the build script runs, then the program's version is the tag, the commit count and the short commit name.
Given the source history has no tags, when the build script runs, then the program's version is the short commit name.
Given someone runs the build script or the release workflow runs it, when it finishes, then the version replaces the empty one in what the program reports.
Given the source is committed, when its version is read, then it is empty, because only a build carries a version.

title: Read and write remembered preferences in the preference store
what: Give the program one place to read and write named preference rows in the preference store, which carries on with defaults when it cannot be reached.
why: Remembered choices must survive between runs, yet an unreachable store must never stop someone from working or interrupt them with alerts.

terms.name: Preference store
terms.means: The place where the program keeps the person's remembered choices between runs; it is not the policy files being edited.

criteria.says: Given the preference store is reachable, when a named preference is saved and read back, then the saved value is returned.
Given the preference store cannot be opened or created, when preferences are read, then they read as their defaults.
Given the preference store cannot be opened or created, when the person changes a preference, then the change is dropped and nothing is remembered at the next run.
Given the preference store cannot be reached, when the program carries on, then the person is not told.

open: Existing settings in the old Windows registry location are not carried over; should a one-time import of them be planned?

title: Keep the person's remembered choices for the rest of the program
what: Give the rest of the program typed access to the remembered choices: the chosen sources, the definitions folder, the language, whether the caution was accepted and whether the offer was considered.
why: Every part of the program that needs a remembered choice gets it the same way, so choices are kept and returned consistently.

terms.name: Remembered choice
terms.means: A decision the person made that the program keeps between runs, such as language or definitions folder; it is not a policy setting.

criteria.says: Given a chosen source, definitions folder, language, caution acceptance or offer consideration is saved, when it is asked for later, then the same choice is returned.
Given a choice was never saved, when it is asked for, then its default is returned.
Given the preference store cannot be reached, when a choice is saved or asked for, then the program carries on with defaults and tells no one.

title: Stamp every built copy with the version of its code
what: When someone runs the build script or the release workflow does, the version is worked out from the code and recorded as a value the Policy Plus API reports, instead of in a generated source file.
why: People can tell which code a copy came from without anyone keeping a version file up to date.

terms.name: Program version
terms.means: The text git gives for the current commit: a tag, commit count and short commit name when tags exist, a short commit name otherwise; it is not the Windows file version or a release name.

criteria.says: Given the code has tags, when the build script runs, then the version is the tag, the commit count and the short commit name that git gives for the current commit.
Given the code has no tags, when the build script runs, then the version is the short commit name that git gives for the current commit.
Given someone runs the build script or the release workflow runs it, when it runs, then the version is worked out from the current commit at that moment.
Given the build script has run, when it finishes, then the version is held as a build-time value rather than written into a generated version source file.
Given the version has been recorded, when the API is asked for its version, then it reports that recorded value.

open: Should the committed code keep any version value, since the old rule says the committed file holds an empty version but the decision drops the generated file?
When the code is exactly at a tag, is the version the tag alone, as git reports it?
Is the build script run automatically with every build, or only when someone or the release workflow runs it?

title: Propose the usual folder and allow another
what: Each time the download screen opens it proposes the Windows policy definitions folder, and a person can pick a different folder instead; cancelling the folder choice leaves the destination as it was.
why: Choosing another folder is rarely needed, so it stays an option the person can use only when wanted, without making it a step of the usual install.

criteria.says: Given the download screen is open and no download is running, when the person chooses a folder in the folder dialog, then the destination is replaced by that folder.
Given the person opens the download screen, when it appears, then the destination shows the Windows policy definitions folder every time and no new policy folder is reported yet.
Given the folder dialog is open, when the person cancels it, then the destination stays unchanged.

title: Install Microsoft's policy definitions in one go
what: A person asks for Microsoft's current policy definitions and the program downloads the one fixed package, installs the templates, the regional-format language files and the English fallback in the destination, and reports the outcome.
why: Administrators get a working set of definitions without finding, unpacking and copying the files by hand, and learn clearly which step failed when something goes wrong.

terms.name: Policy definitions folder
terms.means: The folder where the program reads Microsoft's policy templates and language files from; not the folder holding saved policy settings.

terms.name: Regional format language
terms.means: The language of the person's regional settings, which can differ from the display language; the program installs its language files, with English as the fallback.

terms.name: Scratch folder
terms.means: The temporary folder holding the downloaded package while it is installed; not a place the person keeps files.

journey.name: Install in one go
steps: Wait while the definitions are installed.
Learn the result and use the definitions.

criteria.says: Given a download is running, when the person looks at the start, close, destination and browse controls, then all are disabled so a second download cannot start and the destination cannot change, and they are enabled again when it ends.
Given a download is running, when the person tries to close the download screen, then the close is refused, and given none is running, then the screen closes.

Given the destination folder written in the box already exists and the person is an administrator, when the download starts, then ownership of that folder is taken and Administrators are given full control before any file is moved, whatever folder is written in the box; a standard user skips this, and if taking control fails the download ends with "Failed to take control of the destination." and nothing is moved.

Given the package is downloaded, when it is unpacked and the unpacking fails, then the person is told "Failed to extract the package." and the downloaded package is kept; when it succeeds, the downloaded package is deleted.

Given the package is unpacked, when the files are installed, then the template files go into the destination, the language files of the person's regional format language go into a folder of that name if the package holds one, and unless that language is en-US the English files also go into an en-US folder as a fallback; if the package has no en-US folder, the download stops with "Failed to move the ADMX files." after the destination files were already replaced.

Given files are installed into a folder, when the folder is missing it is created, and every file already there with the same name is deleted and replaced with no backup; only files directly in the source folder are installed, and a failure part-way leaves some files replaced and others not.

Given the person is an administrator, when files are installed, then ownership of the destination and of each existing language folder is taken, a language folder created during the move inherits permissions from the folder above, and every installed file, including the template files in the destination, is reset to inherit permissions; a standard user changes no permissions, and a failure here ends the download with "Failed to move the ADMX files.", not the take-control message.

Given any step fails, when the download ends, then the person is told "Failed to " followed by the failed step, the screen stays open, the controls are enabled again and no policy folder is reported; if only removing the scratch folder fails, the person is told "Failed to remove temporary files." although all files are installed.

Given the download succeeded, when the scratch folder is deleted, then the person is asked "ADMX files downloaded successfully. Open them now?", the destination is reported as the new policy folder only if they answer Yes, and either answer closes the screen as done.

open: The program now downloads and unpacks the package itself rather than with the Windows installer tool: should an unreadable package still end with "Failed to extract the package." and keep the package?
Where the program runs without administrator rights over a protected folder, should the person be told why the install failed beyond "Failed to move the ADMX files."?

title: Offer the missing policy definitions once on first use
what: On the first use of the program, record that the welcome offer has been considered, work out whether this Windows edition lacks the full set of policy definitions, and if so show a single welcome question offering to download them; Yes starts the download.
why: People on editions without Group Policy support get the full set of policy definitions offered without having to notice they are missing, and the offer is considered only once.

terms.name: Orphaned category
terms.means: A category with no parent among the loaded definitions although its definition names one; not a category that simply sits at the top.

terms.name: Empty category
terms.means: A category holding no subcategories and no policies at all, hidden ones counted; not a category whose policies are all hidden.

terms.name: Group Policy support
terms.means: Whether the computer's Windows edition is one of the fixed list of 59 editions that have the Group Policy infrastructure; not whether definitions are loaded.

terms.name: Welcome offer
terms.means: The one question shown on first use offering to download the policy definitions; not the Acquire ADMX Files command in the Help menu.

terms.name: Offer considered
terms.means: The remembered fact that the welcome offer has been weighed on a first use, whether or not it was shown; not the person's answer to it.

journey.name: Offer once, keep it open
steps: Start using the program for the first time
Have missing definitions noticed without having to check
Accept or put off the definitions
Come back to the definitions later

criteria.says: Given the program is shown for the first time, when the welcome offer is considered, then the program records that it has been considered, even when no offer is made, and never considers it again on later starts.
Given a category whose definition names a parent that is not among the loaded definitions, when the program checks for missing definitions, then that category counts as orphaned.
Given a category that holds no subcategories and no policies, even hidden ones, when the program checks for missing definitions, then it counts as empty.

Given the Windows edition reported by the computer is one of the 59 fixed edition codes, then the computer counts as having Group Policy support; given the edition cannot be read, then it counts as having none.

Given the offer is being considered, the edition has no Group Policy support and more than two non-empty categories name a missing parent, when the main window is shown, then the person sees "Welcome to Policy Plus! Home editions do not come with the full set of policy definitions. Would you like to download them now? This can also be done later with Help | Acquire ADMX Files."; otherwise no offer is made.
Given the welcome question is shown, when the person answers Yes, then the download dialog opens.

open: No rule says what happens when the person answers No beyond not downloading; should the program do or say anything more?

The journey asks for a standing invitation to get the definitions later, but no rule or decision states it and today the welcome text only mentions Help | Acquire ADMX Files; should a standing invitation be built, and if so what and where?
The earlier remembered choice lived in the Windows registry and is not carried to the new store; should people who already saw the offer be asked again once?

title: Find each template and its text in the person's language
what: When downloaded definitions are to be used, find the template files in the chosen folder and, for each one, pick the language text that goes with it and read it, refusing flawed language text.
why: A person gets definitions whose names and descriptions read in their own language, and a missing or flawed language is named instead of failing vaguely.

terms.name: Template
terms.means: A definition file describing policies, categories and products; not the language text that names them.

terms.name: Language text
terms.means: The file holding the names, descriptions and screen layouts of a template in one language; not the template itself.

journey.name: Check, then switch
steps: Say that the downloaded definitions should become the ones in use
Be sure each template comes with its text in my language

criteria.says: Given a chosen folder holding template files in any letter case, subfolders and other files, when the definitions are scanned, then only files directly in the folder whose names end in .admx are taken as templates and the rest is ignored.
Given a saved language code, when language text is needed, then that code is used; given none is saved, then the computer's own language is used.

Given a template and several language subfolders, when its language text is chosen, then the subfolder named exactly by the language code is used if it holds this template's file, else the first subfolder of the same language family (compared with capital letters mattering) that holds it, else en-US; a folder lacking the file is skipped.
Given no language file is found in any of those places, when the template is read, then it is refused with "The corresponding ADML is missing" and none of its content is loaded.

Given a language file that cannot be parsed as XML, when it is read, then the template is refused with "The ADML XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>"; given any other read problem, then it is refused with "The ADML is invalid: <detail>".

Given a language file, when its texts are read, then only its first text table is used and each text is kept under its id; given the same text id twice, then the file is refused as invalid and its template is not loaded.

Given a language file, when its screen layouts are read, then only its first presentation table is used; given the same layout id twice, then the file is refused as invalid and its template is not loaded.
Given a language file with no policy resources section, or whose revision is missing or not a number, when it is read, then it is refused as invalid and its template is not loaded.

Given a name or description written as "$(string.<id>)", when it is shown, then the language file's text for that id appears; an unknown id shows the code itself, any other text shows as written and an empty value stays empty.
Given a policy description, when it is prepared for display, then leading and trailing spaces are removed from every line and blank space at the end is dropped.

title: Check every template is sound before using it
what: Read and validate every template beside the current definitions, skipping and listing the ones refused, and stopping at once when a template has no namespace.
why: A bad download cannot spoil the definitions the person already has, and each refused template is named so the person knows what went wrong.

terms.name: Namespace
terms.means: The unique name a template declares for itself so its items stay apart from other templates' items; not a short label, which is only a label inside one template.

criteria.says: Given a template that cannot be parsed as XML, when it is read, then it is refused with "Couldn't load <path>: The ADMX XML couldn't be parsed: <detail>."; given any other read problem, then it is refused with "The ADMX is invalid: <detail>".

Given a template in which any of these is missing or unreadable, when it is checked, then it is refused as invalid: the policy definitions section; the short label or the unique name in a namespace entry; the file name of a superseded older definition; the minimum revision (missing or not a number); a support rule's name or display name; a support reference or range without its reference, or a version bound that is not a whole number; a product's name, display name or version index; a category's name or display name; a category's parent entry or its reference when the category has content; a policy's name, display name, key or class; a policy's category or supported-on reference; a number value's value; a list item's value name; a choice item's display name; or an option's id.

Given a template that declares no target namespace, when the folder is loaded, then loading stops at once with an error, the files after it are not read, nothing is built and the person sees the error text.
Given a template whose namespace is already held by a template loaded earlier, when it is checked, then it is refused with "The <namespace> namespace is already owned by a different ADMX file".

Given a template, when its unique name and short labels are read, then its unique name is the one listed as its target, and each short label it declares must be unique, so a repeated short label refuses the file as invalid.

Given a template's superseded-ADM entry and minimum revision, when they are read, then they are kept when present; an entry without a file name or a minimum revision that is missing or not a number refuses the template as invalid.

Given a category with any content inside it, even a comment, when it is checked, then it must contain a parent entry with a reference or the template is refused as invalid; its explanation is optional.

Given products, when they are read, then three levels are kept (product, major versions, minor versions), deeper levels are not read and each version without a version index refuses the file as invalid.

Given an item in a template, when it is named, then its unique name is the template's unique name, a colon and the item's own name, so equal names in different templates stay apart; given a reference to another item, then a reference containing a colon uses the unique name the template declared for the label before the colon, a label the template did not declare is taken as already complete, and a reference without a colon belongs to the template's own unique name.

Given a setting the template leaves out, when it is read, then it gives nothing; given a setting with a stated default that is left out or whose text is not valid for the kind of value expected, then that default is used.

Given a template refused with a reported failure, when the folder is loaded, then it is skipped and the failure is listed, while the other files still load and the structures are built from those that loaded.

title: Work out categories, products, policies and their options
what: From the validated templates, work out the categories, products, support rules, policies, their options and the screen layouts for entering values, ahead of use, with names and descriptions in the language.
why: The person browses a ready, consistent set of categories and policies, where each policy shows what it applies to and how its options behave.

terms.name: Preference
terms.means: A setting whose registry key lies outside the three policy locations; not a managed policy.

terms.name: Support rule
terms.means: The statement of which products a policy works with; not the products themselves.

criteria.says: Given categories, when they are built, then one with a named parent is attached under it, found in this load or earlier ones; if the parent is not found it has no parent but is still listed among the top-level categories.

Given a policy, when it is built, then it takes its category and 'supported on' rule from the references in its own content and has options only when it contains an options section; it is listed under its named category when found, and otherwise stays in the policy list with no category; it shows the 'supported on' rule its reference names when found, and otherwise none.
Given products, when they are built, then a major or minor version is attached under its parent product defined in the same template, and only products without a parent are top-level.

Given a support rule, when it is built, then it is 'any of' when its first logic element is "or", 'all of' when "and", and blank otherwise; only that first element is read, each reference or range becomes an entry and a range may carry a minimum and maximum version; an entry is linked to the product it names, else to the support rule of that name, else stays unlinked.

Given a policy class, when it is built, then it applies to computers for "Machine", to users for "User", and to both for any other value; a policy applies to an area when its definition declares it, and one declared for both applies to each.

Given a policy's registry key, when its kind is decided, then it is a preference, not a managed policy, when the key is outside the three policy locations ("software, policies", "software, microsoft, windows, currentversion, policies" and "system, currentcontrolset, policies"), and a key counts as a policy key when it is one of those three or lies below one, regardless of case.

Given a registry value in a template, when it is read, then it is a delete marker, a number or a text by the first it contains, a value with none being a delete marker; an option's value name is its own, except a list option with a value prefix attribute (even empty) which uses the prefix, and the own name only when the prefix is empty.

Given the options of a policy, when they are read, then kinds other than number, yes/no, text, list, choice or multi-line text are dropped without notice; a yes/no option takes its registry effect from true and false values and lists; a choice is optional unless marked required and keeps a single value, a list of values or both, and one with neither changes nothing.

Given a number, text or list option, when it is read, then a number accepts 0 to 4,294,967,295 unless the template sets other limits, overwrites existing values unless marked soft and is stored as a number unless marked as text; a text allows 255 characters, is optional, is stored as plain text and overwrites existing values unless the template says otherwise; a list replaces other entries of its key unless marked additive, stores plain text unless marked expandable, numbers entries automatically unless the template says the person names them, and counts as prefixed only when a value prefix is given; unreadable attribute values fall back to these defaults.

Given a policy's settings screen, when it is built, then it has a layout only when the template names one written as "$(presentation.<id>)" and the language file holds that layout; only labels, number boxes, text boxes, check boxes, combo boxes, drop-down lists, list boxes and multi-line text boxes are kept and other controls are dropped without notice; a control keeps the reference id the language file gives it, or has none.

Given the controls of a layout, when they are read, then a number box takes default value 1, shows its up-down spinner and steps by 1 unless the language file says otherwise (an unreadable value falls back to the same defaults), a check box starts unticked unless the language file marks it ticked, a drop-down list has a preselected item only when the language file names one, and combo box and drop-down entries are sorted unless the language file says not to sort them.

Given loaded templates, when they are staged and built, then a template and its language file loaded together stage their categories, products, support rules and policies and are recorded under the template's namespace; when the structures are built the new items join the final lists and staged items are cleared, so loading more files adds to what is available.

title: Switch to the new definitions in one step
what: Once the new definitions are checked, empty the workspace, adopt the checked definitions, remember their folder as the definitions folder and present the category tree clean, with each problem listed.
why: The person lands on a clean, predictable view of the new definitions, with the previous workspace emptied and the downloaded folder remembered.

criteria.says: Given a successful download of definitions with a new folder, when the new definitions are adopted, then the workspace is emptied, the downloaded folder loaded and saved as the definitions folder, and the view rebuilt; given no new folder, then nothing changes.

open: The rules do not say whether the switch is undone as a whole when the definitions folder cannot be remembered.
The rules do not say whether the person sees each problem found while loading, or is asked whether to continue.
The rules do not say that no category, policy or highlighted item is selected after the switch, that the information pane shows its empty message, or that earlier search results are forgotten.

title: Show each policy's state and comment and apply the filters
what: For each policy, work out its state and comment in the shown area or both, and decide whether it is listed, from the chosen area and every active part of the filter.
why: The person sees each policy's setting and comment as before, and the filters keep only the policies they asked for.

terms.name: Only Filtered Policies
terms.means: The switch that limits the list to policies passing the active filter; not the choice of area.

criteria.says: Given both areas are shown and a policy applies to both, when its state is shown, then it reads the common state followed by "(2)" when both match, the computer state followed by "(C)" when only the user is Not Configured, the user state followed by "(U)" when only the computer is Not Configured, and "Mixed" otherwise.

Given a policy that applies to one area, when its state is shown with both areas shown, then it reads that area's state followed by "(C)" for computer or "(U)" for user; with a single area shown, only that area's state appears, without a suffix.
Given both areas are shown, when the comment column is shown, then it is empty when neither area has a comment, shows "(multiple)" when both have one, and otherwise shows the single comment.

Given a chosen area, when a policy is considered for the list, then it is visible only if it applies to a chosen area; with "Only Filtered Policies" on, it must also pass the filter for a chosen area it applies to, and passing for either is enough.
Given a filter on state, when the list is built, then only policies whose state in the checked area is Configured (Enabled or Disabled), Not Configured, Disabled or Enabled, as chosen, are kept.
Given a filter on managed policies, when the list is built, then preferences are hidden when managed policies are wanted and managed policies are hidden when preferences are wanted.
Given a filter on comments, when the list is built, then only policies with a non-empty comment in the checked area, or only those with none, are kept, as chosen.

Given a filter on products, when the list is built, then only policies supported by the chosen products are kept, honouring the options to match any product and to include policies with blank support.
Given several active parts of a filter, when a policy is judged, then it passes only when it passes every active part.

title: Reopen my last policy sources and show everything on start
what: When the program starts, my remembered preferences, the policy sources I used last and their comments are brought back, and the list of policies opens on the broadest view, user and computer policies together.
why: I get back to the policy work where I left it without choosing anything again, and a problem with remembering never stops me.

terms.name: Policy source
terms.means: Where policies are read from and saved to, such as the local Group Policy, a policy file, the registry or a scratch space; it is not the definitions that describe the policies.

criteria.says: Given the program's remembered preferences cannot be kept, when the program starts, then it carries on with the defaults, my changes to preferences are dropped, and I am not told, so nothing is remembered between runs.
Given I have never saved policy sources, when the program starts for the first time, then both the user source and the computer source open as the local Group Policy.

Given the policy sources I saved last time cannot be opened, when the program starts, then I am told "The previous policy sources are not accessible. The defaults will be loaded.", both sources are reset to the local Group Policy and opened without any further message; only the kind of source is reset and any saved location text stays.

Given a source has a place to keep comments, when the program opens it, then its existing comments are brought back, a missing comment file simply means no comments yet, and a source whose comments cannot be read is left without comments.
Given the program has started, when the list of policies is shown, then it is on "User or Computer", so user and computer policies appear together.

title: Tell me once whether the workspace is ready to change
what: After the sources open, one notice names the user and computer sources and says which are fully writable, which can only be viewed and which live only in memory.
why: I know before I start whether my changes will be saved.

terms.name: Fully writable
terms.means: A source whose changes can be saved; not one that can only be viewed or that exists only in memory.

criteria.says: Given a source has just been opened, when the program works out whether I can change it, then a scratch space counts as writable, a registry source counts as not writable when saving a test value to it failed, and any other source counts as not savable when its file could not be opened for writing.

Given a source is described to me, when its state is shown, then it reads "is fully writable", "cannot be saved" (changes work in memory only) or "cannot be modified", and anything other than fully writable counts as a problem.

Given a source is named, when I see its name, then it is one of Local GPO, Registry, File, User GPO, User hive or Scratch space, followed in brackets by its location or the person's account identifier when it has one.

Given the sources have just opened, when either the user source or the computer source is not fully writable, then I am told "Not all policy sources are fully writable." together with the state of both; when both are fully writable, "Both the user and computer policy sources are loaded and writable." is shown only when opening was not quiet, so never when the program starts.

open: Which of "cannot be saved" and "cannot be modified" is shown for a registry source that failed its write test and which for a file source that could not be opened for writing?
Is the status bar name of a source also the name used in the readiness notice?

title: Load the policy definitions I last used and recover from trouble
what: At start the definitions from my saved folder, or the Windows default folder, are loaded; if there are problems I choose whether to keep a partly loaded set or fall back to the default location.
why: The policies I can browse come from the definitions I trust, and a failed load is explained and recoverable.

terms.name: Policy definitions
terms.means: The templates that describe the available policies; not the sources where policy settings are stored.

criteria.says: Given a definitions folder was saved last time, when the program starts, then that folder is loaded; given none was saved, then the Windows default definitions folder is loaded.

Given loading the saved definitions reports problems, when I am asked whether to keep using the workspace, then Yes keeps the partly loaded workspace; No counts as a failed load with the reason "You decided to not use the problematic ADMX bundle.", the partly loaded workspace is thrown away, and what follows is the next two criteria.

Given the saved folder is not the Windows default and fails to load, when I am told "Policy definitions could not be loaded from "<folder>": <reason> Load from the default location?" (the reason is the problem found, or the "You decided..." reason after No), then Yes saves the Windows default folder as my definitions folder and No leaves the workspace empty with no further message.
Given I chose to load the default location, when it loads, then the workspace is replaced by an empty one and the Windows default folder is loaded into it.

Given the Windows default folder itself fails to load (including after I said No to keeping a partly loaded set from it), or fails to load after I chose Yes to the default location, when that happens, then I am told "Policy definitions could not be loaded: <reason>" and the workspace stays empty.

title: Set the language of the policy definition text
what: A person names the language in which policy definition text is shown. The language is checked, remembered at once, and the person is offered a reload so it applies now.
why: Administrators read policy names and explanations in their own language, and they choose when to pay the cost of reloading the workspace.

terms.name: Definition language
terms.means: The language code, two parts around a hyphen such as en-US, that picks the folder the policy definition text is read from; it is not the language of the program's own screens.

journey.name: Name the language, then reload
steps: Say which language the definition text should use
Have the language remembered and applied

criteria.says: Given the language dialog is open, when the person confirms text that does not split into exactly two parts around a hyphen, such as "en" or "en-US-x", then they see "Please enter a valid language code." and the dialog stays open.
Given the language dialog is open, when the person confirms text with exactly one hyphen, such as "en-" or "-", then it is accepted without being checked as a real language code.
Given a language is already stored, when the person enters a code that equals it after spaces are trimmed, with upper and lower case counting as different, then the dialog closes without change.
Given the stored language is en-US, when the person enters en-us, then it counts as a different language and is accepted.
Given the person enters a well formed code that differs from the stored one, when they confirm, then the new code is saved at once.

Given the new language was saved, when the person is asked "Language changes will take effect when ADML files are next loaded. Would you like to reload the workspace now?" and answers yes, then the loaded definitions are emptied and the saved definitions folder is loaded again with the new language.
