open: The language code is later used as a folder name, yet any text with one hyphen is accepted, including text with path characters; should the new product keep accepting it or refuse unsafe text?

When the person answers no to the reload question, the stories state no behaviour for the workspace or for when the language applies; should the workspace stay as it is and the language apply the next time definitions are loaded?

title: Release every open source when the person leaves the program
what: When the person finishes and leaves, every policy source that is open is released on its own, and the person is told only when something could not be released.
why: Finish the work and leave, releasing everything that was opened, without being interrupted unless resources are still held elsewhere.

terms.name: Open source
terms.means: A set of policy definitions the person has loaded to work on, such as a folder, a file or a user's stored settings; not a policy setting itself.

journey.name: Leave and let go
steps: Know if anything was left open

criteria.says: Given the person has policy sources open, when they leave the program, then each open source is released on its own and the program window closes.

Given one of the open sources is a user's stored settings that was loaded for work, when the person leaves the program, then those settings are unloaded and the result says whether unloading succeeded, while every other kind of source is released successfully.

Given every open source released its resources, when the person leaves the program, then no message is shown, because the cleanup message is only given when any source could not release and the step is silent on success.

Given at least one open source could not release its resources, when the person leaves the program, then they are told "Cleanup did not complete fully because the loaded resources are open in other programs."

open: Does the program still close after the cleanup message is shown, or does the person get a chance to stay?
When one open source cannot be released, are the other open sources still released?

Two criteria here (releasing every open source, and unloading a user's loaded settings) come from the journey's recorded steps and from a rule that another story builds; should they be cited here or in that story?

title: Show who made Policy Plus and which version is in use
what: A person can ask the program about itself and is told who made it, where the project is published online and, when the program was built with one, which version it is.
why: People can tell who is behind the program, find its project page, and say which version they run when they report a problem or compare with another copy.

terms.name: About information
terms.means: The short message that names the author, the project address and, when known, the version; it is not the policy description shown for a selected setting.

terms.name: Program version
terms.means: The release label stamped into the program when it was built; it is not the version of the policy definitions that are loaded.

journey.name: Ask who and which version
steps: Find out who made this and which version I have

criteria.says: Given the program is open, when the person asks for the About information, then a message appears that names the author of Policy Plus and the public address of the project.
Given a version was built into the program, when the person asks for the About information, then the message also states that version.
Given no version was built into the program, when the person asks for the About information, then the message names the author and the address and states no version.

open: Should the version shown in the About information be the same stamp that the build records, with nothing shown when the build has none?

title: Choose where user and computer policies are kept
what: The person says where the user policies live and where the computer policies live. For the user side they pick one of local files, the system settings store, a policy file, a particular user's policy, a user profile, or an empty scratch space. For the computer side they pick one of local files, the system settings store, a policy file, or an empty scratch space, because the per-user kinds belong to the user side only. Details are asked only for the kind chosen. They can also back out and leave everything as it was.
why: So the person decides which policies they will read and edit before any work begins, without being asked for details that do not apply to their choice.

terms.name: Policy source
terms.means: The place where one side's policies are kept and read from, such as local files or a policy file; it is not the template that describes what the policies mean.

terms.name: Scratch space
terms.means: An empty source that keeps nothing beyond the session; it is not a saved policy file.

criteria.says: Given the person is choosing the user policy source, when they select a kind that needs a detail (registry path, policy file name, user, or profile file), then only the box and Browse button belonging to that kind can be used and the others stay unavailable.

Given the person is choosing the computer policy source, when they select a kind that needs a detail (registry path or policy file name), then only the box and Browse button belonging to that kind can be used.

Given the person browses for a policy file on either side, when the file picker opens, then it shows only policy files of the right type, lets them name a file that does not exist yet, and does not ask for confirmation when they pick an existing one.
Given the person is choosing sources, when they press Escape, then the dialog closes as cancelled and the sources already open are left as they were.

open: When the person picks the per-user policy kind, which way do they name the user (type the user's identifier, or choose from a list of users), given that the rules only state the identifier is typed?

title: Open the chosen policy sources and keep the view on a visible category
what: When the person confirms, both sources are created from their choices and opened, the result of opening is shown, and the view moves to the nearest category that is visible. The same keeping of the view on a visible category applies whenever a view setting changes: the selection that is no longer shown is dropped and the tree and list are rebuilt. If either source cannot be created, the person is told which side failed and why, and the dialog stays open.
why: So the person starts working against exactly the policies they chose, learns at once, with the reason, when a choice cannot be used, and is never left looking at a category or policy that is no longer shown.

criteria.says: Given the person has chosen a kind for the user side, when they confirm, then the user source is created from it (local files, registry path, policy file, a user's own policy by identifier, a user profile file, or scratch space when nothing else is selected); and if it cannot be created they see "The user policy loader could not be created." followed by the reason and the dialog stays open.

Given the person has chosen a kind for the computer side, when they confirm, then the computer source is created from it (local files, registry path, policy file name, or scratch space when nothing else is selected); and if it cannot be created they see "The computer policy loader could not be created." followed by the reason and the dialog stays open.
Given both sources were created, when the person confirms, then the dialog closes as accepted, the sources are opened, the opening result is shown and the view moves to the nearest visible category.

Given the person changes a view setting, when the view is refreshed, then it moves up to the nearest visible category, drops the selected policy if the move happened or the policy is now hidden, rebuilds the tree and list, and a policy kept appears in the information pane only, with its row not highlighted.

title: Let a person leave the user entry without choosing a user
what: The entry where a person says which user account's own policy is wanted, built so that pressing Escape closes it with no user chosen. Turning a typed name into a security identifier (the account's unique number) and refusing an invalid one is done by the account lookup, built in its own story, which this entry hands the typed text to.
why: A person who opens the entry to name a user can back out with Escape and carry on without having chosen a user.

criteria.says: Given the person is naming a user, when they press Escape, then the entry closes with no user chosen.

open: Should the entry show the translated security identifier to the person before they confirm, as the old dialog did?
Should leaving be possible by other means than Escape, such as a Cancel button?

title: Pick a user profile to use as the policy source
what: A person choosing a user policy source confirms one user profile and gets back the location of that profile's stored settings. They can also leave without choosing.
why: Most people edit their own profile, so the common case needs one confirmation and no searching, while leaving is always possible.

terms.name: User profile
terms.means: A person's own stored settings on the computer, which can serve as the user policy source; not the machine-wide policy settings.

terms.name: Profile settings file
terms.means: The file holding a user profile's stored settings, whose location is returned once a profile is chosen; not the policy source itself.

journey.name: Start from my own profile
steps: Accept or replace the proposed profile

criteria.says: Given the choice of a user profile is open, when the person confirms with no profile selected, then nothing happens.
Given the choice of a user profile is open and a profile is selected, when the person confirms, then the choice closes as accepted and returns the location of that profile's settings file.
Given the choice of a user profile is open, when the person presses Escape, then the choice closes as cancelled.

open: Should the person's own profile be proposed first and the other profiles on the computer be listed, with whether each can be opened now, as the old dialog did? No rule states this.
Should leaving without choosing leave the current policy source unchanged? No rule states this beyond the choice closing as cancelled.

title: Save policy changes to every chosen source in one request
what: The person asks once to save. The system saves the comments, writes each source that can be fully written, makes the change take effect where it can, remembers the chosen sources for next time, and shows one outcome line per source. A local or per-user Group Policy source also gets its version file created or raised so the machine notices the change.
why: Administrators and power users change policy settings and expect them to be kept in their sources and to take effect, without saving each source by hand or guessing what happened to it.

terms.name: Group Policy version file
terms.means: The small file beside a policy file that carries a version number the machine reads to notice a change; it is not the policy file itself.

terms.name: Policy source
terms.means: A place where the user or computer policies are kept, such as a POL file, the registry, a user's registry hive, a user's Group Policy object or the live system; it is not a policy definition.

terms.name: Scratch space
terms.means: A policy source choice whose changes are not kept anywhere; saving it reports that the changes are discarded.

criteria.says: Given comments and policy changes on both the computer and the user source, when the person asks to save, then each source's comments are saved first, then each source that is fully writable is written, then the chosen source types and locations are remembered for the next start.
Given a source that is not fully writable, when the person asks to save, then that source is reported as "not writable" and is not written.
Given the save finishes, when every source saved well, then the person sees "Success." with the user and computer outcomes; when a source fails, then the person sees "Saving failed!" with the reason.

Given a local Group Policy source on a Windows edition that has Group Policy (decided by a fixed list of product edition codes), when the person saves, then its policy file is written, its version file is raised, Windows is asked to refresh policy and the outcome reads "saved to disk and invoked policy refresh".

Given a local Group Policy source on a Windows edition that is not on that fixed list of product edition codes, when the person saves, then its policy file is written, its version file is raised, the difference between the file as last on disk (read at the moment of saving) and the new content is applied to the running account's own registry (the current user's for a user source, the machine's for a machine source), all windows are notified and the outcome reads "saved to disk and applied diff to Registry".

Given a per-user Group Policy object, when the person saves, then its policy file is written, its version file is raised, Windows is asked to refresh user policy and the outcome reads "saved to disk and invoked policy refresh".

Given the person saves, when the source is a POL file, then the outcome reads "saved to disk" and only the file is written; when it is a registry source, then it reads "already applied" because it was changed live; when it is a user hive, then it reads "will apply when policy source is closed"; when it is the Scratch space, then it reads "discarded".

Given a policy file with no version file beside it, when a save raises the version, then a new version file is written with the General section, both extension-name lines for registry policy and version 65537.

Given a version file that already exists, when a save raises the version, then the version rises by 1 for a machine source and by 65536 for a user source, and becomes 65537 when the file holds no version line.

Given a version file that lacks the Machine or User extension-name line for registry policy, when a save raises the version, then the missing line is added and a line already present is left untouched.

open: What should the person see when Windows does not confirm the policy refresh, since the old program ignored that answer and could report a policy as applied when it was not?

If the computer source saves and the user source then fails, should the computer changes stay saved and the chosen sources be remembered, or should the person be told which source failed and what was kept?

journey.name: Save in one go
steps: Ask once to save my changes and see each source's outcome.

title: Show each option's stored value and save it in the right form
what: A policy opens with each option showing the value stored for it, and when it is saved each option's value is stored in the form and place that suits it.
why: The person sees what is really set today, and what they save behaves as the policy expects.

criteria.says: Given a stored number, text or multi-line text is missing or of another kind, when the policy is opened, then it is taken as stored without being checked first.

Given a drop-down choice option, when it is opened, then it shows the first item whose own value is stored and, if the item has a list of values, whose values are all stored; nothing is selected when no item matches.

Given a list option, when it is opened, then a list whose entries are named by the person shows every stored name with its value; and a list whose names do not matter shows the stored values in order: with a name prefix, those named prefix1, prefix2 and so on until the first number that is missing, and without a prefix, every stored value under the list's key.

Given a check box option, when it is opened, then it is ticked when its on value, or every value of its on list, is stored, or, when neither is defined, when its value is 1; otherwise it is unticked, including when its off value is stored.
Given a list of values is looked for in the stored values, when it is checked, then it counts as present only when every value in it is present.
Given a number option is saved, when it is written, then it is stored as text if the definition says to store it as text, otherwise as a whole number.

Given a text option is saved, when it is written, then it is stored as text that can contain variables if the definition says so, otherwise as plain text; and a multi-line text option is stored as a set of lines.

Given a list option is saved, when it is written, then entries with their own names keep them; others are numbered from 1 with the definition's prefix, or named after their own text when there is no prefix.

Given a list option is saved and the definition does not say to keep other entries, when it is written, then every existing value under the list's key is removed first, and a list with no entries stays empty.

Given a check box is saved, when it is written, then a ticked box with no on value first saves 1 and an unticked box with no off value first removes the value; any defined on or off value is then saved with its extra values and replaces that first step.
Given an option names its own location, when it is saved, then it is stored there, otherwise with the policy's other settings.
Given a value is written for a policy and its definition says to delete, then it is removed; a number is saved as a whole number, text as text, and a policy with no value defined writes nothing.

open: What should the person see when a stored number or text is missing or of the wrong kind, since today it is not checked (including multi-line text)?

journey.name: Review what will change
steps: Open the policy with everything already worked out
Say what state it should be in and change only what differs
Confirm, then carry on or finish

title: Change the policy state and options within their limits
what: The person picks Enabled, Disabled or Not configured and edits the options of an enabled policy, with each control accepting only what it allows, and list editing refusing duplicate names.
why: The person can set exactly the values they want and cannot save values the policy cannot hold.

terms.name: List editor
terms.means: The grid in which the person adds, names and removes the entries of a list option; not the policy dialog itself.

criteria.says: Given a number box, when the person types, then only digits and control keys are accepted; other keys are ignored.

Given a number box, when the text is kept, then any text a whole-number reading accepts stays, including a leading sign or spaces; a number over the maximum or under the minimum becomes that limit; other text becomes the default; and a number above 2,147,483,647 becomes the default even when the maximum is higher.

Given a number box, when text is pasted instead of typed, then it is not restricted to digits; and when a negative number is kept because the minimum is below zero, then it is converted to an unsigned number when the policy is applied.
Given a number entered with a spin box, when it is changed, then it stays within the policy's minimum and maximum, moves in the presentation's steps and starts at the presentation's default.
Given a plain text entry, when text is typed, then it is limited to the policy's maximum length and starts with the presentation's default text.

Given a text entry with suggestions, when it is used, then it is limited to the policy's maximum length, starts with the default text and lists the suggestions, sorted unless the presentation turns sorting off.
Given a drop-down list, when it is shown, then it lists the choices by their translated names, sorted unless sorting is off, and preselects the default choice when one is named, otherwise nothing.
Given a check box, when it is first shown, then it starts in the presentation's default state.

Given a list where the person names each entry, when the list editor is confirmed and two names are identical, then it is refused with "Multiple entries are named "<name>"! Remove or rename all but one." and nothing is returned; Run and run count as different names.
Given a list without names, when the list editor is confirmed, then every row except the empty new row at the bottom is returned in the order shown; for named lists the empty new row is also ignored.
Given a list without names, when a row's value cell was never filled in and the list editor is confirmed, then that row is returned as an empty entry.

open: What should the person see when a name cell in a named list was never filled in, which today stops the dialog with an unhandled error?
Should pasted text that is not a number, or a negative number where the minimum is below zero, be accepted as today or refused?
Should a list row with an empty value cell be refused rather than kept as an empty entry?

title: Clear a policy's old settings and write its chosen state
what: When a policy is applied, its old settings are cleared and the chosen state is written: Enabled with its values, Disabled, or Not configured.
why: The policy ends up exactly in the state the person chose, with no leftovers from before.

terms.name: Not configured
terms.means: The policy has no settings in the chosen side; not the same as Disabled, which is a setting of its own.

criteria.says: Given a policy is applied, when its old settings are cleared, then every value it touches is removed from the source, counted once: its own value, its value lists, its options' values, those of check boxes and choices, and the whole key of each list option; the policy then reads as Not configured.

Given the source is a REG file, when a list's whole key is cleared, then its removal entry is dropped if there is one; the request is ignored when a source branch is set and the key lies outside it, and every key is accepted when no branch is set.
Given the source is a policy file, when a list's whole key is cleared, then every "clear all" mark for that key is removed.

Given Enabled is chosen, when the policy is applied, then its own on value is saved, with any extra on values; and when it has a value name but no on value, the number 1 is saved; a list key left blank uses the policy's key.
Given Enabled is chosen, when the policy is applied, then every option of the policy is saved with its current value, including options never filled in.
Given Enabled is chosen and a setting was given no value, when the policy is applied, then that setting is left as it was.
Given Disabled is chosen and the definition gives no off value, when the policy is applied, then the policy's value is removed; a defined off value, with any extra off values, is saved instead.

Given Disabled is chosen, when the policy is applied, then each setting gets only its own removal: all values under a list's key, the saved off value of a check box that has one, and the single value of every other setting; extra values for a chosen item, a check box's on list and the policy's own on list stay.
Given Not configured or an unknown state is chosen, when the policy is applied, then nothing is written or removed beyond the clearing of its old settings.

open: Should the person see a forecast of what saving will change and confirm it before anything is written? No rule describes one, so its layout and whether it can be turned off are undecided.
When Enabled is chosen, which holds when one rule writes every option and another writes only the settings supplied: is a setting left as it was only when the person was never offered it?
Where should the person be told what will happen to the comment when the source holds no comments?

title: Open the policy dialog and finish it with OK, Apply or Cancel
what: A person opens a policy and sees its side, state, supported-on text and comment; OK saves and closes, Apply saves and keeps the dialog open, and Cancel or any other closing still reports a change if anything was applied earlier.
why: One dialog covers looking, saving and leaving, and the rest of the program knows whether anything changed.

terms.name: Policy state
terms.means: Whether a policy is Enabled, Disabled or Not configured in the chosen side; not the values of its options.

terms.name: Side
terms.means: Computer or User: the part of the system a policy setting applies to; not a category of policies.

terms.name: Apply
terms.means: Saves the chosen state now and keeps the policy open; not OK, which also closes it.

terms.name: Save Policies
terms.means: The command that writes all accepted changes to disk; not part of this dialog.

criteria.says: Given a policy that applies to both computer and user, when it is opened without a side, then it can be edited for either and starts on Computer; given a policy for one side only, then it is fixed to that side and the side choice is unavailable. Switching between Computer and User moves the source, whether it can be written to and its comment to that side, and reloads the state from it; option values are replaced only for options that side stores while Enabled, and values typed earlier stay for the others.
Given a policy is opened, when the person looks at the dialog, then the Supported on box shows the policy's supported-on name, or is empty when it names none.
Given a policy is opened, when its present state in the side being edited is Enabled or Disabled, then that state is shown; for anything else, including an unclear state, Not configured is shown.

Given the policy is Enabled, when it is opened, then each option shows what is stored: numbers in number boxes, text in text boxes and combo boxes, the matching item in drop-downs, ticked or unticked check boxes, lines in multi-line boxes and the stored list in the list editor.
Given Disabled or Not configured is chosen, when the person looks at the options, then they are greyed out; they can be edited only while Enabled is chosen.

Given the source holds no comments, when the dialog opens, then the comment box is disabled and reads "Comments unavailable for this policy source"; otherwise it shows the stored comment, or is empty when there is none.
Given the source cannot be written to, when the dialog is open, then OK and Apply are unavailable.

Given the person presses Apply, when the policy is saved, then the dialog stays open and the visit records that a change was made; given the person presses OK, then the policy is saved and the dialog closes as a change.
Given the person presses Cancel, when Apply was used earlier in the visit, then the dialog is reported as a change, and as a cancel otherwise; closing in any other way follows the same rule.

Given a dialog was accepted, when the policy list refreshes, then it updates in place if the current category is still visible, otherwise the program moves up to the nearest visible category; nothing is written to disk until Save Policies.

Given a policy is applied, when it is saved, then everything the source holds for it is cleared first; Enabled then writes every option's current value, Disabled writes the disabled state, and Not configured leaves the policy with no values.
Given the source supports comments, when the policy is applied, then an empty comment box removes the stored comment and any text replaces or adds it.

open: Should leaving with unsaved edits ask the person first, since today Cancel simply discards them?

title: Bring in policy settings text and check it as it arrives
what: A person brings in a semantic policy text, from a file or typed in, and sees at once how many policy settings it holds or the line and reason of the first fault. Nothing is applied in this story.
why: Administrators find out whether a text is good before they offer it to their computer or user policies, without asking for a separate check, and an earlier text or result never lingers.

terms.name: Semantic policy text
terms.means: A plain text script that states, policy by policy, whether each is Enabled, Disabled or Not configured and its settings; it is not a registry file or a policy file.

terms.name: Live check
terms.means: The reading of the text as soon as it arrives, reporting the count of policy settings or the first fault; it is not the apply step and changes nothing.

journey.name: Bring in with live check
steps: Bring in the text, from a file or entered, and see the count or the first fault at once.
Apply what was read, offered only when the text read correctly.

criteria.says: Given the import window is opened, when it opens, then any earlier read result is dropped, so a closed window hands nothing back.

Given the person picks a file, when it is chosen, then the whole file fills the text box, replacing what was there without asking; after a Yes to "Are you sure you want to reset the text box?", the text returns to the header "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and blank lines.

Given text has arrived, when it reads correctly, then the person sees "Validation successful, N policy settings found." and nothing is applied; when it does not, they see "SPOL validation failed: " and the reason.

Given a text whose first line is not 'Policy Plus Semantic Policy', or whose lines are separated by line feeds alone and so read as one line, when it is read, then it is refused with 'Incorrect signature.'.
Given any fault in the text, when it is reported, then the message ends with '(Error found on line N.)' naming the line where reading stopped.

Given a policy header line, when it starts with exactly 'U', then the policy is a user policy; any other first word, including 'u' or 'User', makes it a machine policy, and a header with no space after the first word is refused naming only the line.
Given a policy's state line, when it is 'Not configured', 'Enabled' or 'Disabled' in any letter case, then it is accepted; anything else is refused with 'Unknown policy state.'.
Given a policy that is Not configured or Disabled, when the text is read, then the lines after it are read as the next policy's header and not as settings; settings are read only under Enabled.

Given a setting value, when it is read, then # means a whole number (a non-whole value fails with a conversion message), a plain non-negative number is an unsigned number, 'True' or 'False' in any case is yes/no, single quotes are text, double quotes are a list of text, 'None' is an empty list, and anything else is refused with 'Unknown option data format.'.

Given a bracketed setting, when it is read, then one line is one entry, one text per entry makes a list, two texts make a table of name and value, and no entries stores the setting with no value; for a list setting the existing entries are then removed unless the definition keeps other entries, and nothing is written, and for any other kind of setting the empty value makes the write fail.

Given a comment line, when it is read, then it is recognised in any letter case, a double backslash is one backslash and a backslash followed by 'n' is a line break; a comment ending in a lone backslash is refused with 'Escape sequence started at end of comment.', and a backslash followed by any other character with 'Unknown comment escape sequence' naming it.

Given the text did not read correctly, when the person asks to go on to apply it, then the import window refuses with "The SPOL text is invalid: " and the reason, and hands nothing on; only text that read correctly is passed on.

open: Should the live check also run again after every edit of the typed text, or only when text arrives from a file or is first entered?
Should a text with line feeds alone, which today fails with the signature message, be accepted or get a message that names the cause?
Should an empty bracketed setting be accepted for a list setting without any message, since today it silently removes the existing entries?
Should this refusal still appear when the apply is offered only after the text read correctly, or is the check on the window's own button redundant?

title: Apply a checked semantic policy text to the policy sources
what: From a text that read correctly, the person applies its policies to the computer and user policy sources, and is told the outcome, including how many could not be applied.
why: Administrators move a whole set of settings in at once, and one bad policy does not stop the rest.

terms.name: Apply
terms.means: Writing the policies of a checked text into the computer and user policy sources, replacing each policy's earlier settings; it is not the check, which writes nothing.

criteria.says: Given a text that read correctly, when it is applied, then each policy goes to the computer source or the user source according to its section.
Given a policy is applied, when its earlier settings exist, then they are wiped first and then the stated state and settings are written.

Given a policy comes with a comment and the source keeps comments, when it is applied, then the comment is stored before the old settings are wiped and the new ones written; if the writing then fails, the new comment stays against the half-written policy.
Given a policy comes with an empty comment, when it is applied, then any existing comment is left alone.
Given several policies, when one fails, then it is skipped and counted and the rest are still applied; only the number of failures is known, not which policy or why.

Given the apply has finished, when every policy was written, then the person sees "Semantic Policy successfully applied."; when some failed, they see "N out of M could not be applied."; either way the view refreshes.

open: Should the person be told which policies failed and why, since today only the count is reported?
Should a comment stay against a half-written policy when its writing fails, as today?

title: Copy a policy's settings out as ready-to-use policy text
what: A person looking at a policy's text can choose whether it begins with the Policy Plus heading line and a blank line, or shows only the fragment.
why: People need to take a policy's settings away as text, with the heading included when they want to import it back.

terms.name: Semantic policy text
terms.means: The plain-text form of a policy's settings that can be copied out and imported back; it is not the policy's on-screen description.

terms.name: Policy text heading
terms.means: The heading line "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and a blank line at the top of the text that lets it be imported back; it is not part of the policy's settings.

criteria.says: Given the policy text is shown, when "Include SPOL header" is ticked, then the text starts with the heading "Policy Plus Semantic Policy" and a blank line, followed by the fragment.
Given the policy text is shown, when "Include SPOL header" is not ticked, then only the fragment is shown, without the heading and blank line.
Given the text is shown without the heading, when the person ticks "Include SPOL header", then the heading and blank line appear at the top of the text.

open: When the person chooses Copy, is the whole text as shown (with or without the heading) selected and placed on the clipboard?
When the text window opens, should the text take focus with all of it selected so it can be copied straight away?
Should Ctrl+A select all the text in the box?
Is the heading ticked by default when the text window opens?

title: Arrive at an item by typing its identifier
what: A person types an identifier and is taken straight to the category, policy, product or support definition it names, or is told plainly that it could not be found. The text is trimmed, kinds are tried in a fixed order, and a policy identifier may carry a user or computer ending.
why: Go straight to a known item by typing its identifier, instead of browsing for it.

terms.name: Identifier
terms.means: The text a person types to name one category, product, support definition or policy; not its display name.

terms.name: Section ending
terms.means: An optional "@U" or "@C" at the end of a policy identifier that limits it to the user or computer section; not part of the identifier itself.

journey.name: Type and arrive
steps: Type an identifier and arrive at what it names

criteria.says: Given an identifier with spaces around it, when the person looks it up, then the spaces are ignored and the kinds are tried in the order category, product, support definition, then policy, with the first match chosen and shown with its own icon; a policy is looked up only when no other kind matches.

Given a policy identifier ending in "@U", when it is looked up, then it applies to the user section; given "@C", then the computer section; given no ending or any other ending, then both sections, and the ending is removed before the policy is searched so an unknown ending still finds the policy.

Given an identifier that names a category, when the category is visible, then it opens; when it is not visible, then the person is told "The category is not currently visible. Change the view settings and try again."
Given an identifier that names a policy, when the person arrives at it, then the policy opens in the editor and the policy list moves to it.
Given an identifier that names a product or a support definition, when the person arrives at it, then its details open.
Given an identifier of any other kind of object, when the person arrives at it, then the person is told "That object could not be found."

Given text that matches nothing, when it is looked up, then nothing is selected and a "not found" icon is shown; given empty text, then a blank icon is shown instead; and given text that was a policy and changes to something that is not a policy, then the user or computer section found earlier is not cleared.

Given a policy whose category is visible in the category tree, when the person moves to the policy, then its category is shown and the policy row is selected only if the policy is listed there; given a category that is not visible in the tree, then nothing happens and the person is not told.
Given a policy hidden by the area choice (user, computer or both) or by the filter, when the person moves to it, then its category is shown with nothing selected and no message.

Given the policy list is showing the user or the computer settings, and the policy found by identifier belongs to the user section, the computer section or both, when the policy opens in the editor, then it opens in the computer section if either of the two is computer, otherwise in the user section if either is user, otherwise in both, so Computer wins over User.
Given the policy list, when the person selects an item, then only one item is selected at a time.

open: Should a policy hidden by the area choice or the filter still be selected on arrival, given today it leaves the category shown with nothing selected and no message?

title: Judge whether a support definition is met by the chosen products
what: A support definition lists the products a policy is supported on. The system judges whether a support entry or a whole support definition is met by the products a person has chosen, counting version ranges and nested definitions.
why: Know whether the products a person has chosen are covered by a support definition.

terms.name: Support definition
terms.means: A named list of products and nested definitions that says what a policy is supported on; not a single product.

terms.name: Chosen products
terms.means: The products the person has ticked as the ones that matter when judging support.

terms.name: Any-of matching
terms.means: A way of judging in which a definition that would normally need every entry needs only one; it applies only when it is asked for.

terms.name: Unlisted policies allowed
terms.means: A choice that lets a policy count as supported when it lists no supported-on information.

criteria.says: Given a support entry for a product that is not a version range, when that exact product is among the chosen products, then the entry is met; given a product with versions beneath it, when any of those versions or their sub-products is chosen, then the entry is met even if the product itself is not chosen.

Given a support entry for a product that has versions beneath it, whether a version range or a plain entry for a parent product that is not itself chosen, when any version in its range or a sub-product directly beneath one is chosen, then it is met, the range running from the entry's minimum (0 if none) to its maximum (the highest version if none); a range entry never matches on its own product, and a product with no versions beneath it never matches this way.

Given any-of matching is asked for, when a support definition requires all of its entries, then every entry must be met, and any other definition needs one entry met; given any-of matching is not asked for, then one met entry meets every definition, all-of included; a definition with no entries, or none met, is met only when all are required, and plain product entries are checked before nested definitions.
Given a support definition that has already been met once in one judgement, when it comes up again, then it counts as not met, including when two entries point at the same definition with no cycle.
Given a policy that lists no supported-on information, or a support entry that names no known product, when it is judged, then it counts as supported only if unlisted policies are allowed.

open: Is the rule that a definition met twice counts as not met intended, or an accident of today's code to carry over?
When in the person's journey is a support definition judged, and who chooses the products and whether any-of matching is asked for?

title: Find policies by the words you remember
what: A person types words or phrases they remember and the product finds the policies whose title, description or comments hold them, in both the user and the computer areas, with the option of narrowing where it looks.
why: People often remember what a policy says but not its name or where it sits, so they find it from the words alone.

terms.name: Plain word
terms.means: A typed word with no * or ?, which must appear as a whole word in a text; not a part of a longer word.

terms.name: Wildcard word
terms.means: A typed word containing * or ? that stands for any matching word in a text; not a quoted phrase.

terms.name: Phrase
terms.means: Words typed between double quotes that must appear together as whole words; not several separate plain words.

terms.name: Searched place
terms.means: One of title, description or comment, which the person ticks to say where the words are looked for; not the user or computer area.

journey.name: Search as you type
steps: Say the words or phrases remembered.
Narrow where the words are looked for, if wanted.

criteria.says: Given the person types words, wildcard words (with * or ?) and a quoted phrase separated by spaces, when the search starts, then the words are told apart as plain words, wildcard words and phrases, lowercased, trimmed and cleaned of the characters . , ' " ; / ! ( ) { } [ ].

Given a phrase opens with a double quote, when a later word ends in a double quote, then everything between belongs to one phrase; a single quoted word such as "abc" does not close itself and also takes in the words after it.
Given a phrase was opened with a double quote and never closed, when the search starts, then that phrase is left out and the search is wider than the person may expect.
Given a text, when it is checked, then it is a hit only if it holds every plain word as a whole word, every wildcard word matches some word in it, and every phrase appears as whole words together.
Given a policy and the places chosen, when any one chosen place hits (its title, its description, or a comment on it from the user's or the computer's comments), then the policy is a match.
Given the search text is empty, when the person starts the search, then no search runs and they are told "Please enter search terms."

Given the person has unticked In title, In description and In comment, when they start the search, then no search runs and they see "At least one attribute must be searched. Check one of the boxes and try again."
Given the person has not changed the places to search, when the search screen opens, then In title, In description and In comment are all ticked.
Given words and at least one place are chosen, when the person starts the search, then one search starts with what they entered, over both the user and the computer areas, comments included.

open: The new design says a phrase never closed is told plainly to the person, but the old rule drops it without telling them; which should the product do?

The new design shows results as words are typed, but the old rule starts a search only when Search is pressed; should results appear while typing, and when are an empty text or no chosen place reported?

title: Refuse unusable registry terms and start the search when asked
what: When the person asks to search by registry key and value, the system refuses empty terms and a key that begins with a root key, telling them why, and otherwise starts a search with exactly what they entered.
why: People hear at once, with a clear message, why their terms cannot be searched, and usable terms are never altered.

terms.name: Registry line
terms.means: The single line of text a person gives about a setting, such as a full path ending in a value name; it is not yet divided into key and value.

terms.name: Registry key
terms.means: The path part of a setting that a policy reads or writes; it is not the name of the value held under it.

terms.name: Registry value name
terms.means: The name of one setting held under a key; it is not the key path.

journey.name: One line, split for me
steps: Give whatever is known about the setting
Be told when the terms cannot be used

criteria.says: Given the key and the value are both empty, when the person asks to search, then no search runs and they are told "Please enter search terms."

Given the key text starts with HKLM\, HKCU\, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\ or HKEY_CURRENT_USER\, when the person asks to search, then no search runs and they are told "Policies' root keys are determined only by their section. Remove the root key from the search terms and try again."
Given the terms are usable, when the person asks to search, then a search starts with exactly what they entered.

open: Should the system split one pasted line into a key and a value, and show that reading so the person can correct it? No rule or decision states this.
Should the check for empty terms and a root key run while the person types, or only when they ask to search? The rules state it only when they ask.

title: Match policies to the registry key and value terms entered
what: A policy is shown as a match when at least one setting it reads or writes meets every term the person entered, using wildcard, prefix, whole-name and path-part matching.
why: The person gets the policies that control the setting they named, whether they gave the key, the value name or both.

criteria.says: Given a policy reads or writes several settings, when terms are entered, then the policy matches if at least one setting meets every term, and capital or small letters make no difference.

Given a value-name term without "*" or "?", when policies are searched, then only policies with a setting whose value name equals the term as a whole match; with "*" or "?" those act as wildcards over the whole name.
Given a key term with a backslash and no wildcard, when policies are searched, then policies whose key path starts with that text match.
Given a key term with "*" or "?", when policies are searched, then policies whose whole key path fits that pattern match.
Given a key term with no backslash and no wildcard, when policies are searched, then policies having a key path with a part equal to that text match.

open: Should matching policies appear as soon as usable terms are entered, with no separate request to search? The rules state that a search starts when the person asks.

title: Watch search hits arrive and stop the search when enough is found
what: While a search runs, the person sees each matching policy appear in the results with its category, sees progress as it goes, can stop the search or leave, and is told how the search ended.
why: Review can begin at the first hit instead of after the whole search, and the person always knows whether the results are complete.

terms.name: Search hit
terms.means: A policy that matches the search, shown in the results with its category; not every policy that was checked.

journey.name: Results as they arrive
steps: Watch the policies that match appear as the search goes.
Stop the search once enough has been found, or leave it.

criteria.says: Given earlier results exist, when a new search starts, then the results are cleared, the progress range matches the number of policies and the status reads "Starting search".
Given a search is running, when it tests the policies, then every policy is tested in turn and each hit is added to the list with its category name, in the order policies are held.
Given a search is running, when every 20 policies have been checked, then the list and progress are refreshed and the status reads "Searching: checked N policies so far, found M hits".

Given a search is running, when the person presses Stop or closes the results window, then the search is cancelled; closing before it finished leaves the status at "Search canceled" with the progress bar full.
Given a search ends, when it ends, then the status reads "Finished searching: checked N policies, found M hits", or a "Search canceled" message if it was stopped, and the Stop button is disabled.

title: Pick a search hit to open and step to the next hit
what: From the hits, the person picks one to open its editor in the current area with the policy list moving to it, or moves on to the next hit still shown.
why: Picking is the point of the search, and stepping through hits is how a list of hits is worked.

criteria.says: Given a hit is selected, when the person presses Go or double-clicks it, then that policy is passed back and its position in the results is remembered; with no hit selected nothing is accepted.
Given the person picks a hit, when the results close, then the policy's editor opens in the current area and the policy list moves to that policy.

Given a hit was chosen earlier, when the person asks for the next one (Find Next), then the hit after the last one chosen that is currently shown is taken, skipping hidden ones; when none remains they are told "There are no more results that match the filter."

title: Reopen the last search results without a new search
what: The person can come back to the results of the last search without searching again.
why: People return to the same hits later and should not wait for another search.

criteria.says: Given a search has been run, when the person opens Search Results, then the earlier results are shown again.

open: Should reopening start no new search, reselect the earlier choice if it is still listed, and say "No search has been run yet, so there are no results to display." with nothing opening when there are no results? No rule placed in this plan states these behaviours.

title: Show the limit in force and switch it on or off
what: When a person opens the limit choices, they see the limit now in force: policy type, state, comment status and supported products, with a neutral value wherever the limit has no condition. Changing the limit options turns Only Filtered Policies on, and the person can switch it on or off from its menu; the view moves to the nearest category still shown.
why: A person adjusting the limit starts from what is already narrowing their list instead of a blank form, and is never left looking at a category the limit has emptied.

terms.name: Limit
terms.means: The set of conditions (type, state, comment status, supported products) that narrows the policy list; it is not the choice of user or computer area.

terms.name: Only Filtered Policies
terms.means: The switch that applies or lifts the limit on the policy list; it is not the limit's contents.

journey.name: Live filter
steps: See the limit currently in force.
Choose a policy type, state and comment status.
Be taken to the right place when the limit changes.
Switch the limit on or off without losing it.

criteria.says: Given the limit has no policy-type condition, when the limit choices open, then Policy type shows Any; given it keeps only managed policies, then it shows Policy; given it keeps only the others, then it shows Preference.
Given the limit has no state condition, when the limit choices open, then Current state shows Any; otherwise it shows Not Configured, Configured, Enabled or Disabled as the limit holds.

Given the limit has no comment condition, when the limit choices open, then Commented shows Any; given it keeps only commented policies, then it shows Yes; given only uncommented ones, then it shows No.

Given the limit has a supported-products condition, when the limit choices open, then Supported on is ticked, exactly the limit's products are ticked, both matching options are set as the limit holds, and product branches whose tick differs from their parent are opened.

Given the limit has no supported-products condition, when the limit choices open, then Supported on is unticked, both "Match a policy if at least one selected product is supported" and "Match policies with missing or blank support definitions" are ticked, and no product is ticked.
Given a person changes the limit options, when the change is made, then Only Filtered Policies is turned on and the view moves to the nearest visible category.
Given a person uses the Only Filtered Policies menu, when they switch it on or off, then the limit is applied or lifted and the view moves to the nearest visible category.

title: Narrow the policy list by type, state, comment and products
what: A person chooses a policy type, a state, a comment status and, if wanted, supported products, and when they press OK the new limit holds those choices.
why: People find the policies they need by limiting the list to what they are looking for.

terms.name: Supported on
terms.means: The wish to limit the list to policies supported by chosen products; it is not the policy's own list of supported products.

criteria.says: Given a person has chosen Policy, Preference or Any for type, when they press OK, then the new limit keeps only managed policies, only the others, or has no type condition.
Given a person has chosen Not Configured, Configured, Enabled, Disabled or Any for state, when they press OK, then the new limit requires that state, or has no state condition for Any.
Given a person has chosen Yes, No or Any for Commented, when they press OK, then the new limit keeps only commented policies, only uncommented ones, or has no comment condition.
Given the limit choices are shown, when Supported on is unticked, then the product tree and both matching options cannot be used, and when it is ticked they can be used; they start out unusable.

Given a person ticks or unticks a product by hand, when they do so, then every product beneath it is ticked or unticked to match; given a tick is changed by the choices themselves, then it does not spread.
Given a person presses OK with Supported on ticked, when the new limit is made, then it records every ticked product and both matching options, and it is accepted even when no product is ticked.
Given a person presses OK with Supported on unticked, when the new limit is made, then any ticks and options are discarded and no support condition applies.

open: The plan says the list narrows as each choice is made with no confirming step, but the legacy rules apply the choices when OK is pressed; which moment is wanted?

title: Reset the limit choices or cancel them with Escape
what: A person can return every limit choice to its default in one action, or press Escape to close the choices as cancelled with the current limit unchanged.
why: People need a clean slate and a safe way out of the limit choices.

criteria.says: Given any limit choices are set, when the person resets, then type, state and comment return to Any, Supported on is unticked, both matching options are ticked and no product is ticked.
Given the limit choices are open, when the person presses Escape, then the choices close as cancelled and the current limit is unchanged.

open: The plan says undo puts back the limit held when the person began, but the legacy rule only closes as cancelled with the limit unchanged; if choices narrow the list live, what should undo restore?

title: Open the raw policy editor and work on its entries
what: A person can start editing a policy file directly: a caution is shown the first time, the file's keys and values appear as an ordered tree with only the fitting actions offered, and leaving keeps the changes.
why: Advanced people can reach the raw keys and values of a policy file with a clear warning and a clear answer on whether their changes are kept.

terms.name: Raw policy editing
terms.means: Working directly on the keys and values stored in a policy file; not choosing settings through the policy browser.

terms.name: Deletion entry
terms.means: A special entry in a policy file that marks a value or all values of a key for removal; not an ordinary value.

journey.name: The system picks the area
steps: Start editing the policy file, understanding the risk the first time
Find and work on entries in the file
See what I have changed before leaving, then finish

criteria.says: Given neither the user nor the computer policies come from a policy file, when a person tries to edit a policy file directly, then they are told "Neither loaded source is backed by a POL file."; and given some are, then the area they can pick is limited to those backed by a policy file.
Given the question of which policies to edit is open, when the person looks at the choices, then User and Computer can each be picked only when that choice is switched on for this question.

Given the question of which policies to edit is open, when no choice has been made yet, then confirming does nothing; once User or Computer is chosen, confirming returns that choice and closes the question.
Given the question of which policies to edit is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled.

Given a person has not yet accepted the caution, when they start editing directly, then they see "Caution! This tool is for very advanced users. Improper modifications may result in inconsistencies in policies' states."; choosing Yes continues and remembers the acceptance, and choosing No cancels and asks again next time.

Given the policy file is open, when the entries are shown, then keys appear in alphabetical order ignoring case, each followed by its indented sub-keys and then its values in alphabetical order, and a value with an empty name is not shown.
Given a key has sub-keys, when they are shown, then each sub-key name appears only once regardless of case, and the key itself is never shown among them.

Given the file holds special deletion entries, when they are shown, then "**deletevalues" appears as "Delete values" with its data, "**del.<name>" as "Delete value" with the name, and entries starting "**delvals" as "Delete all values", and none of them can be edited or deleted.

Given the file holds ordinary values, when they are shown, then lists of text show joined by spaces, text as it is, 32-bit and 64-bit numbers in decimal and binary data as hexadecimal bytes separated by spaces, and other kinds show no content.
Given nothing is selected in the list, when the person looks at the actions, then only Add key and Export are available.

Given a key is selected, then Add key, Add value, Delete value, Forget and Export are available and Edit is not; given a value is selected, then Forget is available, Add key, Add value and Export are not, and Edit and Delete value are available only if the value is not already a deletion entry.

Given the person is editing a policy file, when they press Done or Enter, then the editor closes as accepted, and when they press Escape, then it closes as cancelled; there is no Cancel button, and either way every change they made stays on the loaded policies and reaches disk only when policies are saved.

open: When only one of User and Computer is backed by a policy file, is it taken without asking the person?
Is the person shown a summary of what they changed, or a reminder about saving, when they leave the editor?

title: Add a new key to a policy file with its name checked
what: A person adding a key to a policy file gives it a name and is told when the name cannot be used; a usable name creates an empty key under the selected key, or at the top level when nothing is selected, and selects it.
why: The person learns that a name is refused before the key is added, and ends with the new key selected and ready to hold values.

terms.name: Key
terms.means: A named folder in a policy file that holds values and other keys; not a value itself.

journey.name: Checked as you type
steps: Give the new key a name and know at once whether it is usable
Have the key created and selected

criteria.says: Given a key of the same name, ignoring case, already exists under the same parent, when that name is proposed for a new key, then the person is told "The key name is already taken." and no key is added.
Given a name containing a backslash, when it is proposed for a new key, then the person is told "The key name is not valid." and no key is added.
Given the person confirms the name dialog, then the typed name is passed on exactly as typed, without being checked at that point.
Given the person cancels the name dialog, then it is treated the same as an empty name.
Given the name is left empty or the dialog is cancelled, when a key is being added, then nothing is added.
Given a name is given and a key is selected, when the key is added, then an empty key of that name is created under the selected key and is selected in the list.
Given a name is given and nothing is selected, when the key is added, then an empty key of that name is created at the top level and is selected in the list.

open: Is a refused name shown while it is being typed, or only when the person confirms?
When the name box appears, should the cursor be in it with any text already there selected?
Should pressing Escape close the name box as a cancel?

title: Add a new value to a policy file by its name and data together
what: A person adding a value to the selected key chooses its name and one of five kinds, then its data; the value is stored only when the data is confirmed.
why: Today the person is asked for the name and kind in one dialog and then the data in another; this brings name, kind and data together in one pass.

terms.name: Value kind
terms.means: The kind of data a value holds: string, expandable string, list of strings, 32-bit number or 64-bit number; not the value's name.

criteria.says: Given a key is selected, when the person adds a value, then they can choose a name and one of five kinds: String, Expandable string, List of strings, 32-bit DWord and 64-bit QWord, and the kind starts on String.
Given the person confirms the name and kind, then the typed name is used exactly as typed, even if empty, together with the chosen kind.
Given the person cancels, then no name and no kind are returned and no value is stored.
Given a kind is chosen, when the data is first asked for, then the starting data is empty text for a text kind, zero for a number kind and an empty list for a list kind.
Given a name and kind are chosen, when the person has not confirmed the data, then no value is stored; it is stored only once the data is confirmed.
Given a value of the same name already exists in the selected key, when the person confirms the new one, then it is replaced without any warning.

open: Should the kind be suggested from the data (digits suggest a 32-bit number, several lines a list), stay visible and be changeable once name and data are asked together?
Should replacing a same-named value really happen without any warning?

The number limits (0 to 4,294,967,295 for 32-bit, 0 to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615 for 64-bit) and the refusal of unsupported kinds are stated by rules built with the number reader and value editing; does this story need to apply them to a new value's data?

title: Change the data of a value in a policy file in either number form
what: A person picks an existing value in a policy file and types its new data. A number is shown and accepted in decimal or hexadecimal as typed, with both forms shown, so there is no mode to switch. Text and lists of text are entered as such.
why: Administrators editing a policy file directly can correct a value's data without first knowing or switching which number form is on.

terms.name: Value data
terms.means: The content stored in a named value of a policy file, such as a number, a text or a list of texts; it is not the value's name or its kind.

journey.name: Either form accepted
steps: Pick the value and type its new data
Let the system read the number, then keep the change

criteria.says: Given a typed hexadecimal number that is too large to fit, when the person confirms, then the value is set to the largest allowed value.
Given typed text that is not a hexadecimal number, when the person confirms, then the value is left unchanged.
Given new data is confirmed for a value, when the change is kept, then the value's data is replaced by the confirmed data and its name and kind stay the same.
Given new data is confirmed for a value, when the change is kept, then the value stays selected.

open: How does a person mark a typed number as hexadecimal, and how is a number typed without that mark read?
How are the decimal and hexadecimal forms of a number's current data shown together when a value is opened for editing?
What does a person see when they back out of entering new data, and which kinds of value (number, text, list of texts) are entered how?

title: Remove a selected value or key by deletion entry or clearing
what: Let a person mark the value they have selected for deletion, so the policy file keeps an instruction that removes it on the machine.
why: The file keeps a deletion instruction the machine follows when policies are applied, instead of silently losing the value.

terms.name: Deletion entry
terms.means: A value named "**del." followed by the value name, which removes that value on the machine when policies are applied; it is not the same as forgetting the value, which leaves nothing in the file.

journey.name: Straight from the selection
steps: Mark the selected value for deletion
Choose what to do with a selected key

criteria.says: Given a value is deleted from the list, when the person confirms, then the file does not erase it but replaces it with a deletion entry named "**del." followed by the value's name.
Given a value has been replaced by a deletion entry, when policies are applied on the machine, then the value is removed on that machine.
Given the delete dialog for a key has just opened, when the person looks at the choices, then none is chosen, and confirming with none chosen does nothing.
Given the person chooses to clear everything, when they confirm, then the choice is accepted without further input, all values of the key are removed and the key is marked cleared.
Given the person chooses to clear first, when they confirm, then the key is marked cleared and only the direct values it already held are put back.
Given the key holds deletion entries or keys inside it with values, when the person clears first, then those deletion entries are lost and the values of the keys inside it are not put back.
Given the delete dialog is open, when the option to delete one value is chosen, then the value name box can be typed in; when any other option is chosen, then it cannot be typed in.
Given the person chooses to delete one value and leaves the name empty, when they confirm, then it is refused and they are told "You must enter a value name.".

Given the person chooses to delete one value and types a name, when they confirm, then the choice is accepted and any value of that name, whether or not it exists, is removed and replaced by a deletion entry.
Given the delete dialog is open, when the person cancels or presses Escape, then nothing in the file changes.

title: Forget a key or value entirely
what: Let a person remove a key with all its contents, after confirming, or a single value with its deletion entry from the policy file, leaving nothing behind.
why: The policy reverts to saying nothing about what was forgotten, and a whole key is never removed without being asked first.

terms.name: Forget
terms.means: Remove an entry from the file with no deletion instruction left behind; it is not the same as marking a value for deletion.

criteria.says: Given a key is selected, when the person chooses to forget it, then they are asked "Are you sure you want to remove this key and all its contents?".

Given the person is asked to confirm forgetting a key, when they answer Yes, then the key, all keys inside it, every value and every clearing mark are removed from the file with no deletion left behind.
Given the person is asked to confirm forgetting a key, when they answer No, then nothing in the file changes.
Given a value is forgotten, then the value and its deletion entry are both removed from the file the same way.

open: Is anything described or confirmed before a single value is forgotten?

title: Choose an exported settings file and have its key prefix worked out
what: A person starts an import by choosing an exported machine-settings file. The system checks the file is a genuine export, reads its keys, removals, deletions and values, works out the key prefix from the first key, and warns when the file holds default values or the prefix could not be worked out. The person gives a prefix only when none was worked out.
why: The person brings settings from another machine without typing a prefix by hand, and learns at once when the file is not a genuine export or the prefix is unknown. The person can also close the import window with Escape.

terms.name: Exported settings file
terms.means: A text file exported from the machine's settings editor that lists keys and their values; it is not a policy file.

terms.name: Key prefix
terms.means: The leading part of every key name in an exported settings file that is left off when the settings are saved in the policy source; it always ends in a backslash and is not the policy source's own path.

terms.name: Default value
terms.means: A value that belongs to a key but has no name; it is not an ordinary named setting.

terms.name: Top-level section
terms.means: The first part of a key name, such as HKEY_USERS or HKEY_CURRENT_USER, that groups the keys of the machine's settings store; it is not a single key.

journey.name: Prefix worked out for you
steps: Have the file checked and be warned about default values or an unknown prefix
Give a prefix only if the system could not decide one

criteria.says: Given the person is choosing the exported settings file, when the file chooser opens, then only exported settings files are offered.
Given the first line of the chosen file is not the standard export header, when the file is read, then it is refused with the message "Incorrect REG signature".
Given a file with blank lines and lines starting with a semicolon, when it is read, then those lines are ignored.
Given a key heading that starts with a minus sign, when the file is read, then the whole key is marked for removal; otherwise the heading opens a key whose values follow.

Given a value line that starts with an at sign, when the file is read, then it is that key's default value with an empty name, and the file is reported as holding default values when any value has an empty name.

Given a value written as a bare minus sign, as quoted text, as a number, or as raw bytes (whose kind is given in brackets, or plain binary when none is given), when the file is read, then it is read as a value to delete, as text, as a number or as bytes in turn; data in none of these forms is kept as a value with no data and no type, without an error.

Given a chosen file and an empty prefix, when the file is chosen, then the prefix is worked out from the first key only: for a first key that begins with HKEY_USERS it is that top-level section plus the next part of the key, which names a user account; for any other first key, including HKEY_CURRENT_USER, it is the top-level section alone; a first key with no further backslash gives an empty prefix; and a file with no keys gets HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE followed by a backslash.

Given the chosen file holds default values and the prefix was empty, when the prefix is worked out, then the person is warned "This REG file contains data for default values, which cannot be applied to all policy sources."
Given the prefix cannot be worked out, when the file is chosen, then the person is warned only "An error occurred while trying to guess the prefix." and the prefix stays empty.

Given no file is named or no prefix is given, when the person asks to import, then it is refused with "Please specify a REG file to import." or "Please specify the prefix used to fully qualify paths in the REG file." respectively.
Given the import window is open, when the person presses Escape, then the window closes as cancelled.

open: How does the person choose whether the settings go into the user or the computer policy source, and at which point of the import?
Does the person see a summary of what the file contains (keys, removals, deletions, values) and how its keys will be named, before the settings are applied?
Can the person leave in other ways than pressing Escape, and does leaving change anything?

title: Bring the exported settings into the chosen policy source
what: Once a file and a prefix are settled, the person imports the settings into the chosen policy source: marked keys are cleared, marked values are deleted and the others are saved with the prefix left off their names, and what the person sees is refreshed.
why: The settings from the exported file end up in the policy source the person chose, and a failure is reported plainly instead of leaving the person guessing.

criteria.says: Given a file with a key marked for removal, a value marked for deletion and other values, when the import runs, then the key is cleared, the value is deleted and the other values are saved, in the policy source of the area the person chose, and the view is refreshed.

Given a key name that starts with the prefix, whatever its letter case, when the import runs, then it is saved without the prefix; a key that does not start with the prefix is saved with its full original name.

Given a file and a prefix, when the import runs, then the settings are applied straight to the chosen policy source with no further confirmation, and if anything fails the person is told only "Failed to import the REG file."

open: Should a key that does not start with the prefix be refused, or saved under its full name, and is any limit on which parts of the settings store may be written to applied?
A value of an unrecognised form is applied as an empty value or fails; which of the two should the new import do?

title: Import a policy file into the user or computer policy source
what: A person chooses a policy file and the source it belongs to, user or computer, and the system loads the file into that source and says whether it worked. The result is held until the person saves.
why: People can bring in policy settings someone else prepared, in one request, without losing or leaving behind any setting, and without being surprised about what is already stored.

terms.name: Policy file import
terms.means: Loading a chosen policy file into the user or computer source, held in memory; it is not saving to disk.

terms.name: Held change
terms.means: A change kept in memory that reaches disk only when the person saves; it is not a stored change.

criteria.says: Given a readable policy file and a chosen source of user or computer, when the person imports the file, then its settings are applied to that source and the message "POL import successful." is shown.
Given a policy file that cannot be read, when the person imports it, then the message "The POL file could not be loaded." is shown and the source is left unchanged.
Given a policy file imported into a source, when the person has not yet saved, then nothing has reached disk.
Given a whole policy file is imported into a source, when it is applied, then it is applied in full as if the source began empty, so nothing in the file is forgotten.

title: Export a policy source as a registry settings file
what: A person names a file and the system exports the policy source being edited, or just the selected branch of it, as a registry settings file. The branch and the prefix are proposed from what is being edited and can be changed. The person is told whether the export worked.
why: People can carry the settings they edited to machines and tools that read registry settings files, naming only the file in the usual case.

terms.name: Registry settings file
terms.means: A text file of registry keys and values that can be imported on a machine; it is not the binary policy file the person edits.

terms.name: Export branch
terms.means: The part of the policy source that is exported, starting from a key; it is not the whole file unless left empty.

terms.name: Registry prefix
terms.means: The root name written in front of each exported key, such as the current-user or local-machine root; it is not the branch.

journey.name: Export what is selected
steps: Say where to write the exported settings; the branch and prefix are already filled in.
Change the branch or prefix only if the proposed one is not wanted.
Receive the settings file and be told it worked, or back out.

criteria.says: Given the export dialog opens, when it shows its proposals, then the prefix is the current-user root if the user policy source is being edited and the local-machine root otherwise, the branch is the selected key (empty when nothing is selected), and the person can type over either and the text is used as typed; an empty branch exports the whole policy file.
Given no file name is given, when the person asks to export, then the export is refused and they are told "Please specify a filename and path for the exported REG."
Given a branch ending in a backslash is typed, when the export runs, then the trailing backslash is removed before the branch is used.
Given the source is backed by a policy file, when it is exported, then the file is used as it is.

Given the source is backed by the registry (a chosen registry key or a loaded user hive file), when it is exported, then it is rebuilt as a new policy file from the three policy locations of the machine: the policies, the current-version policies and the current-control-set policies.

Given a registry-backed source, when the policy file is rebuilt, then every value and sub-key under each of the three locations is copied with its own data type and environment variables are left unexpanded.
Given keys are marked for removal and values for deletion, when the file is written, then a removed key has a leading minus sign and a deleted value is a bare minus sign.
Given a value with the default name, when the file is written, then it is shown as an at sign; quotes and backslashes in names and text are escaped.
