Given values to write, when the file is written, then text is quoted, a 32-bit number is eight hexadecimal digits marked as a number, and any other type (including a 64-bit number, expandable text or multiple strings) is a series of hexadecimal byte values labelled with its type number, except plain binary which has no type number.
Given a line that would run past the 78th character, when the file is written, then it is broken before that point and each broken line ends with a backslash.

Given the file is written, when the export ends, then the person is told "REG exported successfully." and the dialog closes; on any failure they are told only "Failed to export REG!" and the dialog stays open so they can retry.

Given the dialog is open, when the person presses Escape, then the dialog closes as cancelled. This rests only on the action that closes the dialog as cancelled; no rule states what is or is not written.

open: What should happen when one of the three policy locations does not exist in the registry, given today the copy stops with an unhandled error?
When the person presses Escape and the dialog closes as cancelled, is anything written to the chosen file?

title: Save a policy source out as a policy file
what: A person names the area, user or computer, and the file to write, and the system writes that area's policy source as a policy file, then says whether it worked.
why: Administrators can take the settings of one area out of the program as a policy file to keep, move or apply elsewhere, and are told plainly when the file could not be saved.

terms.name: Policy file
terms.means: A file of policy settings for one area, user or computer, that Group Policy reads.

criteria.says: Given a person has chosen an area and a file to write, when they export, then the area's policy source is written to that file as a policy file.
Given the policy file was written, when the export finishes, then the person sees "POL exported successfully.".
Given the policy file could not be written, when the export finishes, then the person sees "The POL file could not be saved.".

title: Choose the folder of policy definitions to load
what: The person picks one folder of policy definitions from the standard Windows folder, the domain's shared folder when there is one, or a folder of their own. A folder that does not exist is refused when they confirm. They can back out without choosing anything.
why: So that an administrator can point the workspace at the definitions they want to browse without a missing folder being accepted.

terms.name: Definitions folder
terms.means: A folder holding policy definition files and their language texts that the workspace can load; not a policy file or a saved policy source.

terms.name: Domain folder
terms.means: The shared policy definitions folder of the domain the computer has joined; not the standard Windows folder on the computer itself.

criteria.says: Given the person opens the choice of folder, when it appears, then their own folder choice is selected first.
Given the computer has joined a domain and the domain's policy definitions folder exists, when the choice appears, then the domain folder can be selected.
Given the computer has not joined a domain or the domain's policy definitions folder does not exist, when the choice appears, then the domain folder cannot be selected.
Given the standard Windows folder or the domain folder is selected, when the person looks at the folder box and its Browse button, then they cannot be used.
Given the person's own folder choice is selected, when the person looks at the folder box and its Browse button, then they can be used.
Given the person chose the standard Windows folder, the domain folder, or typed a folder, when they press OK, then the folder to load is the one chosen.
Given the person typed a folder that does not exist, when they press OK, then they see "The folder you specified does not exist." and the dialog stays open.
Given the choice of folder is open, when the person presses Escape, then it closes as cancelled with no folder chosen.

open: When the person presses Browse and picks a folder, does it appear in the folder box? No rule states this.
Should the choice show anything when no domain can be reached, beyond the domain folder not being selectable? No rule or decision states it.
Is a missing folder checked before the person presses OK? No rule states an earlier check.

title: Load the chosen folder, replacing or adding to what is loaded
what: Once a folder is accepted, the workspace empties itself first only when replacing, adds the folder without stopping for problems, tells the person if the load fails, and remembers the folder for the next start only when replacing succeeded.
why: So that the person gets their definitions into the workspace in one go, with a sensible default and a clear account of anything that went wrong.

terms.name: Replace
terms.means: Emptying the loaded definitions before loading a folder; not adding the folder to what is already loaded.

terms.name: Remembered folder
terms.means: The definitions folder the workspace loads at the next start; not any folder added on top of the loaded set.

criteria.says: Given the replace option is shown in the dialog for loading a folder, when it first appears, then it is ticked by default.
Given a folder that exists was accepted with OK, when the dialog closes, then the choice of replacing or not is passed on to the load.
Given the person did not accept a folder that exists, when the dialog closes, then no replace choice is passed on.
Given replacing was chosen, when the folder loads, then the workspace is emptied first and the folder's definitions are loaded.
Given replacing was not chosen, when the folder loads, then its definitions are added to the current workspace.
Given the folder has problems, when it loads, then the problems are reported but the load does not stop.
Given loading the folder fails, when the failure happens, then the person is told "The folder could not be fully added to the workspace." with the reason.
Given loading the folder fails, when the person looks at the workspace, then it may be emptied or partly filled and the view is rebuilt anyway.
Given loading the folder fails, when the person next starts, then the remembered folder is unchanged.
Given replacing was chosen and the load did not fail, when the load ends, then the folder is remembered as the definitions folder for the next start.
Given definitions were added to the workspace rather than replaced, when the load ends, then the remembered folder is unchanged.

open: When nothing is loaded, is the person not asked whether to replace? The journey says so, but no rule states it.
Is the replace choice proposed as the default only when something is loaded? No rule states this beyond the option being ticked by default.

title: Add several template files to the loaded policies at once
what: The person chooses one or several policy template files and each is added in turn to the policies already loaded, then sees which were added and which were refused with the reason for each.
why: People can bring extra policies into their workspace in one go without emptying it or changing the folder the program remembers.

terms.name: Template file
terms.means: A single administrative template file (ADMX) holding policy definitions; it is not a folder of templates or a language file.

journey.name: Add several at once
steps: Choose the policy template files to add
See what was added and what was refused

criteria.says: Given the person is adding template files, when the file chooser opens, then it offers administrative template files only and lets them pick one or several (several files extend the single-file choice the program offers today).

Given policies are already loaded, when the person confirms one template file, then that file is added to the loaded policies, which are kept and not emptied (the same file is added alone and the structures are built, as for a single file today).
Given template files were added, when the additions finish, then the folder the program remembers for definitions is unchanged.
Given a chosen file is refused, when the additions finish, then the person sees "The ADMX file could not be added to the workspace." with the reason for that file.

open: Does picking several files extend the single-file rule so that each file is added alone, with one failure reported per refused file?
When several files are chosen and some are refused, are the other files still added?
When several files are refused, are the failures shown together in one message or one after another?
Are the structures built once after all files or after each file?

title: Clear all loaded policy definitions from the workspace
what: A person can close the workspace from the menu, which clears every loaded policy definition at once with no confirmation. Putting back what was cleared after a mistake is planned, but its behaviour is still open.
why: Clearing stays as quick as people expect, and a mistaken clear should no longer mean reloading everything from the folders.

terms.name: Loaded definitions
terms.means: The policy definitions currently open in the workspace for browsing; not the definition files kept in the folders they were read from.

terms.name: Workspace
terms.means: Everything the person has open in the program: the loaded definitions and the previous search results; not the folders the definitions were read from.

terms.name: Previous search results
terms.means: The results of searches run earlier in the workspace; not the policies that are loaded.

journey.name: Clear with a way back
steps: Undo it if it was a mistake.

criteria.says: Given policy definitions are loaded, when the person closes the workspace from the menu, then all loaded definitions are removed at once, no confirmation is asked, and the view is rebuilt.
Given definitions were loaded and a search had been run, when the workspace is closed or replaced by a new one, then all loaded definitions and the previous search results are discarded.

open: The plan adds a new step with no existing rule: after a clear the system says what was removed and restores it on request. What exactly should it say about what was removed?
When the person asks to undo, are the removed definitions loaded again exactly as they were?
Does undo also bring back the previous search results, or only the loaded definitions?
How long is the way back offered: until the next load, until the next action, or for a set time?

title: Review what each loaded template file contributes
what: A person sees the policy template files loaded in the workspace with a summary of what each one defines, and can open one file to see exactly what it defines.
why: So a person can tell which template files are in use and what each adds, without opening every file to find out.

terms.name: Loaded template file
terms.means: A policy template file that has been read into the workspace and whose definitions are in use; not a file that is merely present in a folder.

terms.name: File contribution
terms.means: The policies, categories, products and support rules that one template file defines; not what other loaded files define.

criteria.says: Given a file's details are open, when a person reads them, then they list only the policies, categories (including sub-categories), products (including versions) and support rules that were defined in that file.

open: How does a person open a file's details: by double-clicking it, by pressing Enter on it, or both, and what happens when no file is selected in each case?
What should the list show for each file (name, folder, namespace, counts of policies, categories, products and support rules)?
What should the person see when no template file is loaded?
How does a person get back from a file's details to the list?

title: Choose which policies and categories the tree shows
what: A person narrows the loaded definitions to user policies, computer policies or both, and chooses whether categories with no visible policies are shown.
why: So they see only the part of the definitions they want to read.

terms.name: Area
terms.means: The part of the policies being read: user policies, computer policies or both; it is not the place a policy is saved.

terms.name: Empty category
terms.means: A category that holds no visible policy and no visible subcategory; it is not a category with no policies at all.

criteria.says: Given the definitions are loaded, when the person chooses User as the area, then only user policies are shown.
Given the definitions are loaded, when the person chooses Computer as the area, then only computer policies are shown.
Given the person has chosen User or Computer, when they choose any other area choice, then user and computer policies are shown together.
Given empty categories are hidden, when the person switches empty categories on from the Empty Categories menu, then categories with no visible policies appear in the tree.
Given empty categories are shown, when the person switches them off from the Empty Categories menu, then they leave the tree and the view moves to the nearest visible category.

open: Which area is shown when the person first opens the definitions?
Which category is current when the person first opens the definitions?
Are empty categories shown or hidden when the person first opens the definitions?
Does the area choice also apply to the policies listed beside the tree, or only to the tree itself?

title: Read what a category or policy is for
what: A person moves to a category or points at a policy or category and sees its contents and a description of what it is for, with one focus at a time.
why: So they can move through the loaded definitions and understand each item without opening it.

terms.name: Focus
terms.means: The single category or policy whose description is shown; it is not a record of both a highlighted policy and a highlighted category.

terms.name: Parent row
terms.means: The first row of a category's contents, marked Parent, that leads up to the category above it.

criteria.says: Given the tree is shown, when the person selects a category, then it becomes the current category and no policy stays selected.

Given a category is chosen, when its contents are listed, then an Up row marked Parent that names the parent comes first when the category has a parent, then visible subcategories by name, then visible policies by name.
Given a category is chosen, when its policies are listed, then each policy row shows its state and its comment text.
Given a category is selected or highlighted, when its description is shown, then it carries the category title, the line saying how many policies and subcategories it contains, and its explanation.
Given a category is highlighted but not opened, when its description is shown, then the contents line says "The selected category" and the counts include every policy and subcategory, hidden or not.
Given a policy is selected, when its description is shown, then it carries the policy title, either "Requirements:" with the support name or "(no requirements information)", and its explanation.
Given a policy is a preference, when its description is shown, then a notice says so; for any other policy no such notice appears.

Given a policy is listed, when its icon is chosen, then a preference gets the preference icon, otherwise one with no configurable elements gets the plain icon, otherwise it gets the extra configuration icon.
Given the person highlights a policy, when it is highlighted, then it becomes the selected policy and any highlighted category is cleared.
Given the person highlights a category, when it is highlighted, then any selected policy is cleared and the category is the one highlighted.
Given the person highlights nothing, when the highlight updates, then no policy and no category is highlighted.
Given nothing is selected, when the description pane is shown, then the title and support lines are hidden and the pane reads "Select an item to see its description."

open: Is a policy's description shown as soon as the policy is highlighted?

title: Open an item and offer only the actions that fit it
what: A person opens a category as the current one or a policy for the area shown, by pointer, Enter or right-click menu, and the menu offers only the actions that fit the item.
why: So the same opening works with and without a pointer and the menu offers only what fits the item.

terms.name: Item menu
terms.means: The right-click menu of a category or policy, offering only the actions that fit it; it is not a menu for the whole screen.

criteria.says: Given nothing is selected in the policy list, when the person opens an item, then nothing happens.
Given a category is selected in the policy list, when the person opens it, then it becomes the current category.
Given a policy is selected in the policy list, when the person opens it, then its editor opens for the area currently shown.
Given an item is selected in the policy list, when the person presses Enter, then it opens the same way as when opened directly.
Given a category in the tree, when the person right-clicks it, then it becomes the selected category.
Given a category in the tree, when the person left-clicks it, then the selection is left as it is.
Given the menu is opened from the category tree with a category selected, when it appears, then it is shown for that category.
Given the menu is opened from anywhere else with a row selected in the policy list, when it appears, then it is shown for that row.
Given the menu is opened from anywhere else with no row selected, when the person asks for it, then it is not shown.
Given the menu is shown for a category, when its actions are listed, then policy-only actions are hidden.
Given the menu is shown for a policy, when its actions are listed, then category-only actions are hidden.

open: What should the person see when the menu is requested from the category tree with no category selected? The legacy program fails with an error.

title: Review and merge identical user and computer policies
what: A person can see which user and computer policies are identical, confirm, and have each identical pair become one policy that applies to both, with the number merged reported back.
why: Identical settings that appear twice clutter the list; merging them gives one entry per setting without the person losing anything unseen.

terms.name: Identical pair
terms.means: A user policy and a computer policy that are alone in the same category under the same name, with the same explanation text and the same stored-setting location; not merely similar policies.

terms.name: Both-sections policy
terms.means: A single policy that applies to both users and computers; not a policy of only one section.

journey.name: Review then merge
steps: See which user and computer policies are identical.
Confirm the merge and see how many policies were merged.

criteria.says: Given a user policy and a computer policy that are alone in the same category under the same name and have the same explanation text and the same stored-setting location, when the merge runs, then they become one policy that applies to both users and computers.
Given policies with the same name in the same category whose explanation text or stored-setting location differ, when the merge runs, then they are left as they are.
Given two policies with the same name and details that are both for users, or both for computers, when the merge runs, then they are left as they are.
Given a category that holds more than one policy of that name for a section, when the merge runs, then those policies are left as they are.

Given an identical pair, when the merge runs, then the policy that comes later in the loaded definitions is kept and now applies to both users and computers, and the one that comes earlier is removed.
Given the merge has finished, when the person reads the result, then a message states "Deduplicated N policies." with the number merged.

open: The old program merges at once with no review; the target journey adds a review of the identical pairs and an explicit yes before removal, and a no that changes nothing. Is this confirmed as a new design decision, so it can become criteria?
Should a person be able to leave some listed pairs out of the merge, or is it all pairs or none?
What does the message say when no identical pairs are found: "Deduplicated 0 policies." or no merge offered at all?
After the merge, should the categories and the policy information show the merged policies, and is anything else expected to change on screen?

title: See a policy's section, category and support at a glance
what: Opening a policy shows, in one view, the section it applies to, the category it sits in and the support definition it is supported on, with gaps flagged up front. From there the person can go to the category or the support definition it names.
why: People see what a policy is, where it sits and what it is supported on without searching, and problems such as an orphaned category or missing support are visible immediately.

terms.name: Orphaned policy
terms.means: A policy whose named category does not exist in the loaded definitions; it is not the same as an uncategorized policy, which names no category at all.

terms.name: Missing support
terms.means: A policy that names a support definition which is not in the loaded definitions; it is not the same as a policy with no support named.

criteria.says: Given a policy that applies to both users and computers, when the person opens it, then the section shows "User or computer".
Given a policy that applies to computers only, when the person opens it, then the section shows "Computer"; given one for users only, then it shows "User".
Given a policy in a category that exists, when the person opens it, then the category name is shown and the button to open that category's details is enabled.
Given a policy whose named category does not exist, when the person opens it, then the category reads "<orphaned from " followed by that category code and the category-details button is disabled.
Given a policy with no category code, when the person opens it, then the category reads "<uncategorized>" and the category-details button is disabled.
Given a policy naming a support definition that exists, when the person opens it, then the support definition's name is shown and the support-details button is enabled.

Given a policy naming a support definition that does not exist, when the person opens it, then the support text reads "<missing: " followed by the code the policy names and the support-details button is disabled.
Given a policy that names no support definition, when the person opens it, then the support text is blank.
Given the policy view with an existing category, when the person chooses the category-details button, then the details of that category open.
Given the policy view with an existing support definition, when the person chooses the support-details button, then the details of that support definition open.

open: The rules do not say whether the support-details button is enabled or disabled when a policy names no support definition; which should it be?

title: Show a category's parent and let people go up to it
what: Open a category from the category list, or the category a policy sits in, and see its details with its parent's name and a way to go to the parent in the same window.
why: People can see where a category belongs and move to its parent, and a parent that has gone missing is shown as such instead of leading nowhere.

terms.name: Orphaned category
terms.means: A category whose named parent cannot be found among the loaded definitions; it is not a top-level category, which names no parent at all.

criteria.says: Given a category whose parent exists, when the person opens its details from the category list or from the category a policy sits in, then the details show the parent's name.
Given a category whose parent exists, when the person looks at its details, then the button to go to the parent is available.
Given a category whose parent is named but missing from the loaded definitions, when the person opens its details, then the parent shows as "<orphaned from <parent name>>" instead of a name.
Given a category whose parent is named but missing, when the person looks at its details, then the button to go to the parent is disabled.
Given a top-level category, when the person opens its details, then no parent is shown.
Given the details of a category whose parent exists, when the person chooses to go to the parent, then the same window shows that parent's details.

journey.name: Whole ancestry at once
steps: Open a category and see where it sits in the whole tree.
Jump to any parent in the chain.

open: Should the details also list the policies the category holds?
Should the details show the whole chain of parents at once, instead of one parent at a time?

title: Browse products, their versions and details in one view
what: Show every loaded product with its number of children, open a product to see its major and minor versions together, and read the details of any product, version, child or parent in place.
why: People can see a whole product family and read each item without narrowing list by list.

terms.name: Product family
terms.means: A product together with its major and minor versions; not a single version on its own.

criteria.says: Given definitions are loaded, when the person opens the product browser, then every loaded product is listed ordered by name, each with its number of children.

Given a product is selected, when the major versions are shown, then they are the children of that product ordered by version, under a heading naming the product; with none selected the list is empty and asks the person to select one.

Given a major version is selected, when the minor versions are shown, then they are the children of that major version ordered by version, under a heading naming it; with none selected the list is empty and asks the person to select one.
Given no product is selected in a list, when the person double-clicks or presses Enter, then nothing happens.
Given a product with children is shown, when its details are read, then every child is listed with its version and name; a product with no children shows an empty list.
Given a child is listed in the details, when the person double-clicks it, then that child's details replace the current ones in the same view; with nothing selected, nothing happens.

Given a product has a parent, when its details are shown, then the parent name is shown and the button to go to the parent is enabled; given it has none, the parent is blank and the button is disabled.
Given a major or minor version is shown, then its version number is shown; given a top-level product is shown, then the version is blank.
Given a product is shown, then it is labelled "Major revision", "Minor revision" or "Top-level product" according to its type.

open: What happens when the person chooses the parent button: are the parent's details shown in the same window?
What happens when a product is selected and the person double-clicks it or presses Enter: are its details shown?

title: Browse the support rules and see which products they cover
what: The person narrows the list of support rules by name, opens one to see how it matches products and which products or nested support rules it names, and follows an entry to the product details or to the nested rule in the same place.
why: People can find the support rules by name and see which products and nested rules each one names.

terms.name: Support rule
terms.means: A named definition saying which products a policy works with, by matching all or any of them; it is not a policy or a product.

journey.name: Start from the product
steps: Say which name I care about
Open a support rule and see which products it covers
Follow an entry to its product or nested rule

criteria.says: Given support rules are loaded, when the person types text in the filter, then only support rules whose name contains the text are shown, whatever the upper or lower case; with no text every support rule is listed, ordered by name with leading spaces ignored and not shown.

Given a support rule has entries, when its details are shown, then each entry is listed by the name of the nested support rule, otherwise the name of the product, otherwise as "<missing: " followed by the product code it names; minimum and maximum versions are listed only for product entries that name a version range, a missing bound blank.

Given a support rule is shown, when the person reads its details, then it states "Match all the referenced products", "Match any of the referenced products", or "Do not match products" when it has no matching logic.

Given the person double-clicks an entry in the support rule details, when it is a product entry, then the product details are opened; when it is a nested support rule, then that rule is shown in the same window; when its product is missing or nothing is selected, then nothing happens.

open: Should a person be able to narrow the support rules by the product they care about, not only by name, and which rule would say how?
Should opening a support rule by double-click or Enter, and doing nothing when none is chosen, be stated as a rule, since no rule states it today?

title: Inspect a policy's stored setting and presentation, and copy a line
what: Let someone open a policy and read a plain summary of what it stores and where, then ask for the presentation and element detail only when wanted, and copy a selected line of the inspection.
why: Most readers want the gist of a policy before the detail, so the technical makeup stays one request away instead of in the way.

terms.name: Inspection
terms.means: The technical view of one policy showing what it stores, its presentation and elements and its semantic text; it is not the plain description shown when browsing.

criteria.says: Given a policy that names a registry value, when someone opens its inspection, then the summary shows a "Registry value" line; given it names none, then no such line appears.
Given a policy that names a client extension, when someone opens its inspection, then the summary shows a "Client extension" line; given it names none, then no such line appears.

Given a policy with both a presentation and elements, when someone asks for the presentation detail, then the details are listed whatever the elements hold, and each presentation item with an ID shows the details of the element with the same ID, while items without an ID show none.
Given a choice element, when its detail is shown, then the choice names come from the definitions file that defines the policy, and the choices are numbered from zero in the order of that file.

Given a list element, when its detail is shown, then it says "User provides value names" if the person names the values, the prefix if the element has one, and otherwise "No prefix (values named for their data)".

Given a group of affected registry settings with no on or off setting, when the detail is shown, then it reads "Left implicit" if the policy names a registry value and "Left to elements" if it names none; inside a Yes/No element it always reads "Left implicit".
Given a line is selected in the inspection, when someone presses Ctrl+C, then that line is placed on the clipboard.
Given no line is selected in the inspection, when someone presses Ctrl+C, then nothing is copied.

open: What should the inspection show when a presentation item names an element ID that no element has, given the old program stopped with an unhandled error?

title: Show a policy's semantic text on request
what: Let someone ask for the semantic text of a policy, written one section per area the policy applies to, only when they want it.
why: The written form of a policy's settings is detail most readers do not need, so it is shown only on request.

terms.name: Semantic text
terms.means: The written form of a policy's settings, one section per area, that can be moved in and out of the program; it is not the registry file form.

criteria.says: Given a policy that applies to computers, users or both, when someone asks for its semantic text, then there is one section per area it applies to, reading that area's stored settings and comment, and an area the policy does not cover is left out.
Given a section of semantic text, when it is written, then its heading line starts with C for a computer policy or U for a user policy, followed by the policy identifier.
Given a policy that is not Enabled, when its semantic text is written, then its settings and option values are left out; given it is Enabled, then they are listed.
Given a policy with a stored comment, when its semantic text is written, then the comment appears in that section; given none is stored, then no comment appears.

Given option values in semantic text, when they are written, then a whole number has a leading #, an unsigned number is plain digits, yes/no is True or False, text sits between single quotes, an empty list reads 'None', a list of text is bracketed with one double-quoted item per line and any quote inside an item is doubled, and a table is bracketed as double-quoted name: value lines.
Given text option values that hold a quote or a line break, when the semantic text is written, then the text is written between single quotes with no escaping, so it cannot be read back correctly.

Given a comment with backslashes or Windows line breaks, when the semantic text is written, then each backslash is doubled and each carriage return plus line feed pair is written as \n, while a lone line feed or lone carriage return is written as it is.
Given a comment holding a lone line feed or a lone carriage return, when the semantic text is written, then the comment is split over two script lines and is corrupted when read back.

open: Should semantic text that holds a quote or a line break that cannot be read back be flagged to the person, as the step describes, and in what words?
